items.text: The system must secure the objective necessity of synthetic a priori cognition without deriving it from experience or extending it into cognition of supersensible objects.
Objectivity is reconstructed as lawful determination within possible experience rather than correspondence established by pure thought alone.
Sensible givenness and conceptual unity become cognitively effective only through a mediating architecture joining receptivity, synthesis, and apperception.
Judgment and temporal schematization transform categories from formally available concepts into rules applicable to appearances.
Schematized categories generate a system of principles that determines the universal form and quantitative organization of possible experience without anticipating empirical content.
The conditions that constitute phenomenal objectivity also restrict valid cognition to phenomena, making constitution and limitation two functions of one mechanism.
The movement is recursively spiral: categories demand mediation, mediation produces experience, experience validates categorical employment, and that validation reinstates experiential restriction.
Closure remains critical and finite: empirical objectivity is secured, empirical determination remains open, and the supersensible survives only as a negative boundary.
[Persistent] Objective cognition requires the conjunction of sensible givenness and conceptual determination; neither receptivity nor thought has independent cognitive sufficiency.
[Persistent] Objectivity consists in necessary rule-governed synthesis through which appearances become determinately cognizable objects.
[Attractor] Possible experience is simultaneously the ground of objective validity, the field of legitimate application, and the limit of finite cognition.
[Mutating] Categories change from empty logical forms into objectively determining rules only through sensible and temporal specification.
[Mutating] Productive imagination supplies the mediating synthesis whose function is subsequently inherited by schema and subsumption.
[Persistent] A priori necessity establishes objectivity only by expressing necessary conditions of possible experience, not by origin, formal consistency, or subjective compulsion alone.
[Emergent] Systematic cognition depends on preserving the functional differences among sensibility, intuition, imagination, understanding, judgment, and reason.
[Mutating] Validity is an application-relation completed through judgment, although no universally mechanical rule can eliminate judgment from subsumption.
[Emergent] Truth is distributed across heterogeneous registers: logical admissibility, analytical recognition, transcendental validity, and synthetic object-determination.
[Terminal] Pure understanding legislates the universal form of lawful nature but cannot anticipate particular empirical laws, qualities, or causes.
[Mutating] The finite subject is the functional source of synthetic unity while remaining sensibly and temporally non-coincident with its determining activity.
[Emergent] Constitution and restriction are inseparable: the conditions producing experiential objects also prohibit their conversion into things as cognized independently of experience.
[Emergent] The category table becomes a generative system whose schematized forms yield the principial architecture of possible experience.
[Terminal] Positive noumenal cognition collapses, while the negative noumenon persists as an indispensable but indeterminate limit-concept.
The category retains its identity as a pure rule of unity but changes from empty conceptual form into a schematized principle of experiential determination.
Intuition persists as object-givenness, expands into the synthesized spatial-temporal manifold, and is absorbed into quantitative phenomenal determination.
Possible experience expands from an epistemic restriction into the jurisdictional attractor coordinating validity, application, principles, and limitation.
Imagination first appears as explicit mediation and then recedes as schema inherits its application-function.
Time shifts from a form of intuition and self-affection into the universal medium of schematization, while being excluded from the definition of logical contradiction.
Judgment reverses from an irreducible natural capacity into a restrictedly regulable transcendental operation without becoming algorithmic.
A priori necessity reverses its apparent expansionary force and becomes authoritative by accepting the limits imposed by possible experience.
Nature emerges from generalized perceptual synthesis as formally necessary lawfulness while remaining materially open to empirical determination.
Noumenon changes from a candidate supersensible object into a split concept whose positive sense disappears and whose negative sense remains structurally indispensable.
Particular temporal schemata remain lower-layer application machinery; the current-level proposition is that every objective categorial use requires sensible specification.
Pedagogical examples and exercises remain local illustrations of judgment’s irreducibility and do not ground transcendental validity.
Noncontradiction remains a local formal gate, while the distinction between logical admissibility and synthetic objectivity scales upward into a differentiated theory of truth.
Extensive and intensive quantity remain regional determinations of appearances, but they demonstrate globally that a priori form can govern phenomena without determining things in themselves.
Faculty distinctions scale upward from local taxonomy into a jurisdictional architecture assigning different validity-functions to receptivity, understanding, judgment, and reason.
Imagination, judgment, and schematism bridge the lower-layer units by successively specifying how pure concepts acquire sensible application.
Positive ontology is superseded by an analytic of understanding’s conditions, powers, and limits.
Categorical completeness becomes a current-level systemic dependency, although its proof remains presupposed rather than reconstructed.
Thought is not cognition because concepts cannot generate the givenness of their objects.
Sensibility is not self-sufficient because an unsynthesized manifold does not yet constitute an objective perception.
Empirical derivation and subjective preformation cannot account for the objective necessity of categories.
Formal consistency is not a sufficient criterion of truth, objective possibility, or synthetic grounding.
No complete algorithm of application can replace judgment, because every application-rule reproduces the problem of subsumption.
Categories cannot determine objects beyond sensible conditions, regardless of their a priori origin or logical persistence.
Phenomena and noumena cannot form two symmetrical domains of positive cognition.
Universal formal lawfulness cannot yield particular empirical qualities, causes, laws, or existence.
The architecture cannot admit a fully constituted cognizable object-domain prior to sensible givenness and synthesis.
The source, formal possession, and valid application of a concept cannot be treated as equivalent.
No single faculty or formal principle can absorb the heterogeneous functions required for objective cognition.
No standpoint is available from which appearances and the same objects independently of sensibility could be compared.
The mediating operation cannot become wholly transparent without ceasing to perform the bridge-function the system requires from it.
The system cannot admit positive transcendental ontology without collapsing the distinction between logical categories and valid object-reference.
Systematic completeness cannot survive the abandonment of categorical completeness, even though the latter is not independently secured at this scale.
Intellectual intuition is the unavailable possibility that would eliminate the heterogeneity of concept and givenness but is denied to finite cognition.
The common ground of spontaneity and receptivity is structurally required but cannot itself become an object of cognition.
The system is organized around the absence of any external comparison standpoint capable of validating appearance against independently cognized intrinsic reality.
The noumenal remainder can be neither positively cognized nor eliminated, because either operation would destroy its limiting function.
Unconditioned cognitive closure is unavailable: formal necessity cannot become complete possession of reality.
Categorial validity requires both constitution of the phenomenal object through synthesis and controlled application of the category through judgment.
Schematism regulates transcendental application without eliminating judgment’s irreducibility, so mediation directs rather than mechanizes subsumption.
The principial system converts formal natural lawfulness into determinate experiential possibility while leaving empirical specification irreducible to pure understanding.
Logical admissibility and objective possibility form distinct thresholds because consistency can preserve a judgment without supplying intuition, schema, or object-reference.
The subject’s role as synthetic center does not yield intellectual self-possession, because its activity becomes cognizable only through receptive temporal appearance.
Productive imagination becomes structurally more indispensable as it becomes textually less explicit, since schema inherits but does not independently generate its mediation.
Critical limitation is a positive organizational operation because it distributes cognitive authority and stabilizes the negative noumenon as a boundary.
Phenomenal continuity can block inferences to simples or absolute void without licensing claims about the intrinsic constitution of all reality.
Cognitive authority becomes conditional power: a priori principles acquire necessity precisely by accepting finite conditions of valid use.
Constitution and limitation are one recursive event rather than successive independent operations.
Phenomenal objectivity is subject-conditioned without being arbitrary because its conditions are universally necessary for possible experience rather than privately associative.
Time becomes both the medium of objective application and the form through which the subject fails to achieve immediate self-coincidence.
Metaphysics becomes jurisdictional analysis of object-reference rather than positive cognition of supersensible entities.
Nature is closed with respect to universal experiential form but open with respect to its particular empirical determinations.
The capacity of thought to exceed intuition is not eliminated but converted into the recurring possibility of transcendental illusion.
The unknown remainder is generated internally by successful phenomenal constitution rather than imported as a second positive world.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Empty category → demand for intuition → synthesis → experience → categorical validation → renewed restriction to experience forms the primary recursive loop.
Understanding requires sensibility for objects, while sensibility requires understanding for objective unity; their reciprocal insufficiency generates cognition.
Rules produce the application problem, higher-order rules reproduce it, and schematized judgment interrupts but does not abolish the regress.
Mediation changes phase from imagination to temporal schema to systematic principles without losing its function as the bridge between heterogeneous representations.
Possible experience is the dominant attractor because objectivity, necessity, application, systematicity, and limitation all return to it.
A priori independence produces the temptation of unrestricted application, whose failure recursively reinstates the experiential boundary.
Noumenon operates as a limit-loop: abstraction opens a supersensible position, absent intellectual intuition empties it, and the empty position returns as a boundary.
The category table generates principles, principles organize experience, and the requirement of object-reference returns to constrain the categories that generated them.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Pure concept and sensible manifold begin as heterogeneous conditions incapable of independently determining an object.
Sensible givenness → spatial-temporal manifold → imaginative synthesis → apperceptive unity.
Apperceptive unity → lawful perception → possible experience → phenomenal objecthood.
Judgment and temporal schema convert categorial form into rules for subsuming appearances.
Schematized categories → category-generated principles → universal formal determination of experience.
Formal determination divides into mathematical construction of intuition and dynamical connection of phenomenal existence.
Universal experiential form preserves empirical inquiry because pure principles cannot supply determinate qualities, causes, existence, or particular laws.
Attempted transcendental extension → loss of sensible application → collapse of positive ontology → negative noumenal closure.
Pure conceptual availability → distinction between thought and cognition → demand for object-givenness.
Object-givenness → sensible manifold → synthetic unity → phenomenal perception.
Phenomenal perception → possible experience → objective validity of categories.
Categorical validity → application problem → judgment and temporal schematization.
Schematization → principial system → formal and quantitative organization of nature.
Principial organization → empirical underdetermination → continued inquiry within formal lawfulness.
Secured empirical objectivity → test of jurisdiction → exclusion of transcendent employment → negative noumenal boundary.
The opposition between subjective conditions and objective validity collapses within phenomena because universally necessary subjective synthesis constitutes phenomenal objectivity.
Objectivity is reclassified from correspondence available to pure thought into jurisdictionally valid synthesis under conditions of givenness.
Possibility divides into logical noncontradiction and objective possibility grounded in intuition, schema, and possible experience.
Truth becomes a stratified field rather than a single criterion applicable equally to analytical and synthetic cognition.
A priori status is separated from unrestricted range, making critical restriction constitutive of authority rather than external to it.
Nature divides into invariant formal lawfulness and empirically discoverable material determination.
Metaphysics is redrawn as analysis of application, jurisdiction, and limit rather than cognition of objects in general.
The two-world model is replaced by an asymmetry between a cognizable phenomenal field and an indeterminate limiting remainder.
At the surface level, categories, intuition, judgment, schemata, principles, quantity, nature, and noumenon are coordinated around the problem of valid object-reference.
At the structural level, cognition is generated through the distributed cooperation of receptivity, imagination, apperception, understanding, and judgment.
At the metastrategic level, critique redistributes cognitive authority by distinguishing valid empirical employment from formal semblance and transcendental misuse.
At the ontological and temporal level, reality-for-cognition is phenomenal, rule-governed, continuous, and temporally mediated, while intrinsic reality remains indeterminate.
At the methodological and performative level, the system repeatedly constructs a valid cognitive mechanism and then derives its limits from that mechanism’s conditions.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Judgment must remain irreducible to rules while transcendental schematism claims to regulate pure conceptual application.
Objective reality requires object-givenness, yet merely possible experience is treated as sufficient for validating a priori cognition.
The unity attributed to formal intuition remains unstable against the claim that perceptual unity derives from synthesis not belonging to sensibility alone.
Time is treated as the universal medium of schematization even though external objectivity irreducibly requires space.
The systematic completeness of the principles depends on an exhaustive category table whose completeness is presupposed at this scale.
Productive imagination is indispensable to mediation but becomes increasingly opaque as its function is transferred to schema and principle.
The thing in itself must be thought as the limit of appearance, although every determinate cognition of it is prohibited.
The category mutates from logical form into a temporal rule and then into a principle of possible experience.
Objectivity mutates from apparent correspondence into lawful synthesizability and finally into a jurisdiction of valid application.
Necessity mutates from formal or subjective compulsion into determination by conditions of possible experience.
A priori independence reverses from an apparent warrant for expansion into the reason unrestricted employment must be constrained.
Mediation mutates from imaginative synthesis into schematic subsumption while preserving its bridge-function.
Noumenon mutates from an ambiguous candidate object into a split concept whose positive sense collapses and whose negative sense survives.
Critique mutates from negative prohibition into the positive jurisdictional architecture distributing cognitive validity.
Reality-for-cognition is a gated synthesis engine through which only sensibly given manifolds can become objects under schematic and categorial unification.
The subject is a finite switching-center between receptivity and spontaneity rather than an independent creator of its manifold.
Time is the transformation medium through which synthesis becomes application, quantity, experience, and incomplete self-presence.
The phenomenal field is a continuous lawful interior bordered by an unknowable remainder rather than a self-contained totality.
Legitimate navigation consists in routing claims through intuition, schema, synthesis, and experiential jurisdiction instead of escaping toward supersensible possession.
The extracted axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the current-level movement from heterogeneous cognitive conditions through mediation and principial objectivity to critical limitation.
Reconstruction remains underdetermined concerning particular schemata, the developed principles of relation and modality, and the proof of categorical completeness.
The architecture is coherent only if logical possibility, objective possibility, transcendental meaning, empirical validity, and noumenal limitation remain distinct.
The architecture is strongest where the same mediating conditions explain both the generation of experiential objectivity and the restriction of cognitive jurisdiction.
Reconstruction preserves the system only by retaining its recursive sequencing, concealed mediation, empirical openness, and terminal negative remainder.

items.text: The system must secure objective cognition while adjudicating reason’s demand for totality without allowing either conceptual coherence or rational inference to become supersensible knowledge.
Cognition is generated by a differentiated faculty architecture in which sensibility gives, understanding synthesizes, and reason systematizes without collapsing into either lower faculty.
Necessary synthesis first converts perceptions into objects, after which rational recursion converts every conditioned cognition into a demand for further conditions.
Possible experience operates simultaneously as the positive field of objective validity and the boundary against constitutive transcendence.
The unconditioned is generated as the necessary horizon of rational completion precisely where it remains unavailable as an experiential object.
Dialectical illusion arises when subjective or logical necessity is transferred into objective determination without the sensible conditions required for cognition.
Critique preserves reason’s necessary excess by reallocating it from speculative ontology into regulative systematization, practical orientation, and reciprocal dogmatic restraint.
The movement is recursively critical: each positive construction generates a scope-limit, each limit exposes a new rational excess, and each excess returns cognition to critical regulation.
Closure remains nonterminal because critique can discipline assent but cannot eliminate the rational demand that regenerates transcendental illusion.
[Persistent] Objective validity requires sensible givenness, lawful synthesis, and restriction to the conditions under which an object can enter possible experience.
[Persistent] Sensibility, understanding, and reason possess irreducible functions whose coordination generates cognition without licensing their mutual substitution.
[Attractor] Possible experience is both the sole positive domain of theoretical object-determination and the criterion limiting the objective use of principles.
[Persistent] Reason necessarily ascends from conditioned cognition toward an unconditioned completion that experience cannot supply.
[Mutating] The unconditioned changes from a demanded terminus into a horizon, a triadic architecture of ideas, and finally a taxonomy of dialectical problems.
[Emergent] Logical form is simultaneously the grammar through which reason organizes totality and the vehicle through which rational functions are falsely projected into ontology.
[Persistent] Subjective necessity, inferential inevitability, and rational demand never establish objective knowledge without corresponding conditions of intuition.
[Emergent] Validity differentiates into constitutive object-cognition, regulative systematic unity, and practical orientation without permitting speculative hypostatization.
[Mutating] The experiential boundary changes from a prohibition against transcendence into a productive operator that secures objectivity and allocates reason’s nonconstitutive uses.
[Mutating] Subjectivity divides into an empirically determinable self dependent on external relations and a transcendental subject required for cognition but unavailable as a determinate object.
[Attractor] Critique is recurrent self-limitation rather than final correction because transcendental illusion survives disclosure of its invalidity.
[Emergent] Time divides into a phenomenal order constructed through lawful relations and a rational temporality kept open by regress, approximation, and noncompletion.
[Terminal] Failed speculative doctrine terminates not in an opposed ontology but in boundary-discipline, reciprocal restraint, and practically oriented commitment.
[Attractor] Possible experience and the unavailable unconditioned form coupled poles: one determines what cognition can possess, while the other perpetually organizes what reason must seek.
[Stable identity] The distinction between sensibility and understanding persists, while reason is added as a non-object-determining faculty of systematic totalization.
[Functional recurrence] Possible experience retains its limiting function but expands from a domain of objectivity into a juridical and allocative criterion for reason’s uses.
[Escalation] Reason changes from an organizer of rules into a totalizing engine whose lawful drive toward unity generates systematic overreach.
[Mutation] The unconditioned moves from demanded completion through triadic differentiation to the absent attractor of dialectical regulation.
[Mutation] The idea changes from taxonomic conception into practical archetype, regulative rule, dialectical premise, and finally disciplined orientation.
[Reversal] Logical form changes from the architecture of rational systematization into the medium of its own ontological misuse.
[Escalation] Critique changes from local diagnosis into permanent regulation once illusion is recognized as structurally recurrent.
[Displacement] The empirical self dependent on external permanence is displaced at the dialectical level by an indispensable but indeterminate transcendental subject.
[Reversal] Nonempirical status changes from apparent absence of objectivity into the enabling condition of regulative and practical efficacy.
[Absorption] The negative noumenon is absorbed into the general boundary of category-use, while the unconditioned assumes the distinct dynamic role of reason’s unattainable horizon.
[Domain bifurcation] Time changes from an unavailable medium reconstructed through phenomenal relations into a recursive structure of rational regress and open approximation.
[Local] Reflection-concepts and the differentiated table of nothing remain diagnostic instruments; only the general provenance-test scales into the current architecture.
[Scales upward] The temporal analogies scale from determinate principles of experience into the positive relational ground presupposed by every later rational totalization.
[Bridge] The local account of sensory error scales into a general grammar in which subjective determination is projected as objective ground.
[Bridge] The derivation of ideas from syllogistic forms remains classificatory machinery, but it bridges rational totalization and the taxonomy of dialectical error.
[Scales upward] Reciprocal legal freedom remains a local example, while the priority of practical norms over empirical institutions becomes current-level architecture.
[Underdetermined] Antinomy and ideal remain taxonomic branches because only paralogism receives detailed diagnostic execution.
[Catalyst] The attribution of objective reality catalyzes the transition from a general theory of rational ideas to the concrete diagnosis of self-objectification.
[Superseded] Rational psychology loses its status as positive science and survives only as a negative discipline restraining opposed dogmatisms.
[Local] Introductory titles and sectional designations remain insufficient to establish doctrine, though their insufficiency reinforces the prohibition against deriving content from form alone.
Logical thinkability, noncontradiction, and inferential validity do not establish objective possibility or existence.
Categories and rational concepts cannot determine objects independently of intuition and the conditions of possible experience.
Subjective rational necessity cannot be converted into objective necessity in things.
Inner consciousness supplies neither a self-sufficient temporal ground nor knowledge of substantial personal persistence.
The unconditioned cannot appear as an empirically presentable object within the field it is invoked to complete.
Transcendental illusion is neither accidental nor eliminable through heightened attention or intelligence.
The failure of one speculative doctrine cannot establish its contrary or restore an exhaustive opposition between rival metaphysical systems.
Practical necessity cannot be converted into theoretical cognition of supersensible objects.
Empirical institutions and prevailing conduct cannot supply the measure by which their own normative legitimacy is judged.
The architecture cannot admit a homogeneous cognitive continuum in which sensibility, understanding, and reason differ only by degree.
No standpoint is available from which finite cognition can inspect things in themselves or possess the complete series of conditions.
The system excludes a theoretically transparent subject capable of converting its indispensable cognitive function into self-intuition.
No critical achievement can guarantee immunity from the recurrence of transcendent projection.
The architecture cannot reduce empirical objectivity, practical authority, and regulative legitimacy to one homogeneous form of validity.
Conditions required for experience cannot be converted into determinations of supersensible being by abstraction from their sensible use.
The rational demand for completion cannot be abolished without also abolishing reason’s system-producing function.
Neither empiricist exhaustion of validity by sensible presentation nor dogmatic possession of supersensible objects is admissible.
The system is organized around the unavailable possibility of an intuition adequate to the unconditioned.
The nonappearance of time is the absence around which phenomenal succession, persistence, and coexistence must be synthetically reconstructed.
Reason’s demand for absolute completion lacks any adequate presentation through which completion could become objectively verified.
No self-grounding inward bearer is available to unify empirical selfhood and transcendental subjectivity into a knowable substance.
The absent reconciliation between rational ideal and complete realization sustains practical approximation rather than terminating it.
The system denies both final rational self-transparency and any position external to reason from which dialectic could be permanently terminated.
The positive construction of empirical objectivity supplies the criterion by which reason’s ideas are denied constitutive object-use without being abolished.
The boundary of possible experience is productive in both directions: it secures phenomenal cognition and reclassifies rational excess as regulative or practical.
Once temporal synthesis constitutes one law-governed nature, reason can escalate that conditioned unity into the idea of a world-totality without thereby cognizing the totality as given.
The provenance-test governing categories expands into a general diagnosis of dialectic: subjective rational grounds become illusory when projected as objective determinations.
Because empirical self-determination depends on external permanence while transcendental subjectivity cannot become an intuited object, no self-sufficient inward substance can unify both levels.
Necessary synthesis and systematic unity have asymmetrical validity: the former constitutes experiential objects, while the latter regulates the ordering of already constituted cognition.
Nonpresentation changes valence across the architecture: it disqualifies constitutive object-knowledge but enables ideas to function as practical and regulative orientations.
Since illusion survives its critical exposure, successful boundary-setting necessarily becomes a recurrent practice of monitoring rather than a completed correction.
Speculative limitation protects a practical domain from theoretical disproof but does not itself generate the positive warrant of practical efficacy.
Noumenon and unconditioned converge as unavailable limits but remain functionally distinct: the former marks categorial restriction, whereas the latter drives rational totalization.
The system of reason becomes a topology of validity, limits, operations, and recurrent failures rather than an inventory of independently cognized metaphysical beings.
Constitutive objectivity and regulative totality are asymmetrical products of cognition: synthesis determines objects, while reason organizes their cognition toward an unavailable completion.
The subject becomes structurally divided between an empirical node within phenomenal relations and an indispensable condition that cannot know itself as substance.
Time acquires two nonidentical forms: objective phenomenal time reconstructed through relations and rational time recursively opened by regress, reform, and approximation.
Metaphysics is reclassified from cognition of supersensible beings into an immanent diagnosis of how logical functions become hypostatized predicates.
Critical limits operate positively by securing phenomenal objectivity, differentiating valid uses, and preventing rational orientation from hardening into ontology.
Noncompletion becomes generative because unavailable totality drives continued systematization while unrealized ideals sustain continued practical approximation.
Critical agency becomes navigation among differentiated validity-conditions rather than possession of either a final system or an external standpoint.
Practical judgment gains critical priority over empirical actuality because institutions are assessed by ideals they can approximate but never exhaust.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: The objectivity loop moves from representation through provenance and synthesis to valid experience, then returns every successful determination to a renewed test of scope.
The rational regress recodes each achieved condition as conditioned, thereby regenerating the demand for an unconditioned completion.
The boundary loop blocks constitutive transcendence and returns reason’s excess as regulative systematization or practical orientation.
The illusion loop converts rational demand into objective projection, exposes the projection, disciplines assent, and then restarts because its generative conditions persist.
The self-objectification loop attempts to derive subject-unity through categories that already presuppose that unity.
The practical approximation loop judges actuality by an unrealized ideal, produces reform, and renews the ideal’s authority through noncompletion.
Triadic rational totalization branches into subject, world, and supreme being, while the subject-branch escalates substance into simplicity, personality, permanence, and immortality.
Possible experience and the absent unconditioned form a coupled attractor-system: cognition repeatedly returns to the first while reason repeatedly exceeds it toward the second.
The idea becomes a machine when its movement from rational horizon to practical archetype, regulative rule, dialectical premise, and disciplinary problem begins generating further transformations.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Sensible givenness + schematized synthesis + apperceptive unity → objectively valid experience.
Permanence + causal succession + reciprocal coexistence → one temporally unified phenomenal nature.
Conditioned cognition + recursive search for grounds → demand for unconditioned completion.
Unconditioned demand + syllogistic distribution → ideas of subject, world, and supreme being.
Absence of corresponding intuition → failure of objective deduction → prohibition of constitutive transcendence.
Transfer of logical function into object-predicate → objective attribution → dialectical illusion and paralogistic ontology.
Critical adjudication → separation of constitutive, regulative, and practical validity → preservation of rational excess without hypostatization.
Persistent illusion + blocked speculative closure → recurrent vigilance, systematic approximation, practical orientation, and reciprocal restraint.

Sensible givenness → lawful synthesis → unified nature → possible experience → rational regress → unconditioned horizon → triadic ideas → objective projection → dialectical illusion → critical allocation → recurrent vigilance.
Faculty-confusion → transfer of subjective or logical necessity → self-objectification → paralogistic ontology → intuition-test → speculative collapse → boundary-discipline and practical relocation.
Logical validity and objective validity become distinct levels, preventing formal coherence from carrying automatic ontological commitment.
Possible experience is remapped from a mere empirical limit into both the positive domain of objects and an allocative boundary for rational functions.
The opposition between rational order and rational error collapses because reason’s lawful demand for unity also generates dialectical illusion.
The opposition between empirical objecthood and fiction collapses because nonempirical ideas can possess regulative or practical validity without becoming presentable objects.
The subject is remapped from a self-grounding inward substance into an externally conditioned empirical node and a formally indispensable but indeterminate transcendental function.
Time is remapped from an absolute container and terminal progression into phenomenal relational order and recursive rational noncompletion.
Psychology, cosmology, and theology are reclassified from independent object-domains into differentiated outputs of one totalizing operation.
Critique is redefined from rival doctrine or eradication of error into navigational regulation, boundary-discipline, and controlled reassignment of rational excess.
At the surface level, the system tests reflection-concepts, temporal analogies, modality, rational ideas, the metaphysical triad, and the soul-predicates of paralogism.
At the structural level, sensible presentation and understanding constitute objects while reason recursively organizes conditioned cognition toward totality.
At the metastrategic level, critique assigns legitimate uses, exposes unauthorized transfers between validity-levels, and converts final correction into permanent vigilance.
At the ontological and temporal level, reality is a relational phenomenal field whose grounds cannot be possessed, while reason remains divided between backward regress and forward approximation.
At the methodological and performative level, the system repeatedly generates valid cognition, produces rational excess, restricts that excess, and preserves it in transformed use.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reason must seek completion to organize cognition, yet every constitutive objectification of that completion violates the conditions of objective knowledge.
Logical form performs indispensable generative and taxonomic work even though the logical-transcendental analogy authorizing that work remains incompletely demonstrated.
The system requires a criterion distinguishing subjective rational maxims from objective principles, but the operational form of that criterion remains underspecified.
Practical ideas are assigned efficacy after speculative cognition fails, yet the positive mechanism warranting that efficacy remains external or underdetermined.
The positive theory of experience contains compressed transitions from temporal conditions to complete reciprocity and from required permanence to external matter.
The triadic architecture claims systematic reach while antinomy and ideal remain undeveloped relative to the detailed treatment of paralogism.
Noumenon and unconditioned converge as unavailable limits, but identifying them would collapse a categorial boundary into a dynamically generated rational horizon.
Reflection mutates from a local diagnostic of comparison-concepts into the universal provenance-test governing objective claims and dialectical projections.
Possible experience mutates from the positive domain of objectivity into a juridical boundary and then an allocative operator for differentiated validity.
The idea mutates from taxonomic designation into practical archetype, regulative concept, and systematic taxonomy of reason’s intrinsic errors.
The subject mutates from an externally conditioned empirical self into the indeterminate center of a paralogistic construction.
Critique mutates from corrective decomposition into permanent regulation and boundary-discipline.
Validity mutates from empirical objective reality into differentiated practical authority and regulative legitimacy.
Rational psychology mutates from positive doctrine into a boundary-discipline whose trans-experiential claims are relocated rather than theoretically vindicated.
Reality is a field of conditioned presentations organized into experience while recursively referred toward a final condition that cannot appear within it.
Cognition is a layered conversion machine whose objective channel produces experience and whose rational engine projects unavailable completion as apparent objecthood.
The subject is both a relational node within phenomenal nature and an indispensable but blind operational center incapable of self-intuition.
Time is an absent phenomenal coordinate reconstructed through relations and a rational asymmetry between demanded grounds and open consequences.
Navigation remains possible through provenance-testing, intuition-testing, boundary allocation, and approximation, while escape into positively cognized supersensible reality remains disallowed.

The extracted axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the movement from experiential objectivity through rational totalization to dialectical illusion, critical restriction, and transformed rational use.
The positive mechanisms of practical efficacy and determinate regulative guidance remain underdetermined, as do the undeveloped operations of antinomy and ideal.

The architecture is coherent if experiential objectivity and rational orientation remain differentiated while the same restriction explains both the impossibility of transcendence and its recurrent illusion.
The architecture is strongest where independent analyses of objective synthesis, rational projection, and the determining-versus-determinable subject converge on one boundary logic.

Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if positive constitution, recursive excess, triadic differentiation, concrete self-objectification, and disciplinary reversal remain sequentially connected.

Complete axiomatic closure remains unavailable because analogical overextensions, the logical-transcendental homology, practical warrant, and the relation between empirical and transcendental subjectivity resist final reduction.

items.text: The system must reconcile reason’s necessary demand for unconditioned cosmological completion with the impossibility of cognizing the world-whole as a given object.
Categorial synthesis becomes cosmological only where regressively ordered conditions can be totalized across composition, division, causality, and dependence.
Antinomy arises when reason’s demand for completeness converts appearances and their successive conditions into a completed world existing in itself.
Contradiction therefore diagnoses a misclassified scope and a shared invalid object-model rather than contradictory properties of the world.
Possible experience becomes the criterion of speculative objectivity, while lawful experiential integration preserves empirical reality without independent subsistence.
Cosmological totality is displaced from a terminal object into a regulative rule directing the continued search for conditions.
Noncompletion is differentiated by modes of synthesis: homogeneous mathematical series prohibit an unconditioned member, while dynamical dependence may conditionally admit a nonempirical ground.
The movement is recursive and spiral: category becomes idea, idea is objectified into antinomy, critique dissolves the objectification, and the demand returns as regulated inquiry.
Closure is critical rather than cosmological: reason preserves its regulative demand by renouncing total possession and widening empirical correction.
[Persistent] Every conditioned appearance necessarily activates reason’s demand to seek the unconditioned totality of its conditions.
[Persistent] Speculative objectivity is authorized only where an object can be related to lawful possible experience.
[Persistent] Spatial-temporal objects are appearances whose empirical reality does not entail self-subsistent transcendental reality.
[Mutating] Cosmological totality changes from a presumed terminal object into a regulative principle governing inquiry.
[Persistent] Phenomenal conditions are available through successive synthesis, never as a complete regress already given.
[Emergent] Antinomy is generated when recurrent rational totalization converts conditioned appearances into a completed cosmological object.
[Attractor] Contradiction has critical force because it exposes the false object presupposed by opposed cosmological judgments.
[Terminal] The phenomenal world-whole cannot legitimately bear finite, infinite, simple, composite, free, necessitated, or absolutely dependent determinations.
[Mutating] Empirical regress is necessarily nonterminal, but its form varies between indefinite extension and infinite divisibility according to the synthesis involved.
[Emergent] Homogeneous mathematical series exclude an unconditioned member, whereas dynamical synthesis may admit a heterogeneous ground only if empirical lawfulness remains uninterrupted.
[Attractor] The unconditioned remains an unattainable terminus that orders the search for conditions without becoming its empirical endpoint.
[Terminal] Critical self-limitation is reason’s positive completion because prohibition is converted into systematic empirical correction and extension.
[Attractor] Transcendental illusion survives exposure, so critique must recur as vigilance rather than conclude in permanent emancipation from totalization.
[Persistent] The logical necessity of seeking conditions cannot legislate the ontological constitution of the world.
Categories retain their identity as forms of understanding but acquire a second career when reason converts their conditioned use into cosmological totalization.
Totality reverses from the intended endpoint of explanation into a regulative idea preventing arbitrary empirical arrest.
The unconditioned mutates from a supposed grounding terminus into an unattainable horizon and finally a selective gate for admissible explanation.
The world is displaced from a completed object into an open field constituted through possible synthesis.
Contradiction changes valence from pure reason’s endogenous self-conflict into diagnostic evidence of an invalid object-model.
Skepticism reverses from surrender or oscillation into a cathartic instrument against dogmatic question-formation.
Possible experience escalates from a restriction on claims into the criterion of objective reality and the dominant attractor of critical adjudication.
Infinity ceases to name one cosmological magnitude and splits into operational forms of continuation and inexhaustible determinability.
Transcendental idealism changes from a distinction between appearances and things in themselves into the active diagnostic mechanism dissolving antinomy.
Architectonic closure reverses into critical closure, replacing metaphysical completion with a regulative method of self-limitation.
An intellectual condition shifts from an illicit substitute terminating empirical regress into a conditionally admissible nonmember of a dynamical series.
Practical and architectonic interests disappear after explaining allegiance because they cannot survive as criteria of speculative validity.
Syllogistic classification and taxonomies of partisan interest remain local diagnostic machinery rather than governing principles of the meta-cluster.
The detailed proofs of individual antinomies remain local demonstrations and compression points whose asymmetries do not determine the global architecture.
The four cosmological domains scale upward only as differentiated manifestations of one totalizing operator.
The serial-subordination criterion bridges categories to cosmological fields but is subsequently absorbed into the broader structure of conditioned regress.
The distinction between appearances and things in themselves scales globally because it withdraws the completed object-domain presupposed by every antinomy.
Finite and infinite remain local exemplary predicates, while their joint invalidity scales into a general critique of world-totality predication.
The technical distinction between indefinite and infinite regress scales upward by replacing the finite-infinite binary with a synthesis-sensitive typology.
The mathematical-dynamical distinction becomes a transition catalyst because it separates reciprocal rejection from qualified admissibility.
The intelligible condition bridges critique to dynamical reconciliation but remains subordinate to empirical continuity and derivative admissibility.
Practical and architectonic interests become obsolete once inquiry transfers from motivation to objective validity.
The world-whole is not an experiential object, and no standpoint outside possible experience may survey it.
Rational necessity does not establish objective existence or authorize transition beyond experiential conditions.
The complete phenomenal condition-series cannot be presupposed as pregiven.
Explanation cannot terminate arbitrarily in an absolute empirical boundary, first condition, or final datum.
Dogmatic selection and skeptical surrender are excluded as terminal responses to antinomial conflict.
Empirical idealism and transcendental realism are jointly rejected: objects remain empirically real without becoming independent spatial-temporal things.
Inexhaustible regress never establishes actual infinity in the object.
An intelligible ground cannot function as a covert phenomenal member or competitive empirical cause.
Practical need and partisan interest cannot serve as logical criteria of speculative truth.
Formal opposition does not guarantee objective reference for either cosmological alternative.
No standpoint external to possible experience can occupy or survey the completed series of conditions.
The logical form of explanation cannot be identified with the ontological structure of its empirical object.
No single model of totality can govern every mode through which conditions are given or synthesized.
Appearances cannot be compared with or converted into spatial-temporal things existing independently of sensibility.
No completed explanation or metaphysical inventory can furnish cosmological reason with a final endpoint.
The boundary of experience can authorize neither transcendent speculation nor ontological denial of what cannot appear.
Critique cannot permanently extinguish the rational generator of transcendental illusion.
No self-transparent subject can occupy the transcendental exterior denied to cosmological cognition.
The deepest organizing absence is an intuition in which the world-whole and all its conditions are given at once.
Reason’s demand for the unconditioned can never coincide with a completed sensuous presentation of totality.
No admissible exterior can become either a survey-position over the world or an exception interrupting empirical lawfulness.
The system is organized around an end that must regulate cognition while remaining unavailable to cognition.
No guaranteed correspondence joins reason’s necessary demand for completion to a final metaphysical object.
Permanent repose and final metaphysical inventory are structurally excluded.
The positive character of an intelligible dynamical condition remains the unnamed absence required by qualified reconciliation.
The four antinomies are necessary conflict-outputs of serial totalization, yet critique reclassifies them as tests of objective validity rather than descriptions of the world.
Once the shared assumption of a self-subsistent completed world is withdrawn, thesis and antithesis can become jointly invalid rather than exhaustively contradictory.
Deobjectifying cosmological totality preserves rather than destroys empirical objectivity because objectivity depends on lawful synthesis, not independent subsistence.
Because illusion recurs while totality survives as a rule, critique must remain iterative rather than culminate in a final correction.
Open-ended regress does not have one cosmological meaning; its legitimate form varies with the synthesis and givenness of conditions.
The prohibition on importing an intellectual terminus into empirical regress is compatible with a noncompetitive intelligible ground only after mathematical and dynamical synthesis are distinguished.
Antinomial failure can indirectly confirm transcendental ideality, but this metacritical proof risks circularity because it relies on the framework it claims to confirm.
Critical prohibition acquires positive force when methodological empiricism converts the impossibility of total possession into regulated expansion of experience.
Practical interests can survive speculative limitation without authorizing cosmological knowledge, although their non-dogmatic relation to reason remains unsettled.
The original bifurcation between complete series and first condition is recoded by synthesis-type into mathematical reciprocal invalidity and dynamical conditional admissibility.
Categories acquire a threefold career: they organize legitimate experience, generate dialectical illusion when totalized, and return as constraints on regulative inquiry.
Cosmology becomes a metadiscipline governing the conduct and limits of explanation rather than a doctrine inventorying world-properties.
Objectivity becomes temporal and procedural because objects are lawfully synthesized while total synthesis remains unavailable.
The world becomes a task-structured field and horizon of regress rather than an object whose total content can be simultaneously possessed.
The rational subject becomes both generator and tribunal of illusion, but only as a finite regressor situated within experience.
Cosmological time becomes an asymmetrical open procedure: antecedent conditions are required, but their total past cannot be given as complete.
Infinity is redistributed from an intrinsic world-property into differentiated permissions for continuation, division, and noncompletion.
Contradiction becomes metacritical evidence that the alleged object has been falsely constructed.
Critical authority shifts from metaphysical possession to the correction and extension of empirical cognition.
Supersensible grounding receives only derivative admissibility and cannot become a covert interruption of empirical explanation.
Agency becomes situated correction and navigation within experience rather than sovereignty over its totality.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Conditioned appearance generates a demand for a condition, and each attained empirical condition regenerates the demand.
The primary escalation converts category into idea, idea into paired demonstration, and demonstration into critical diagnosis.
The principal capture loop moves from demand for conditions to reification of totality and antinomial breakdown.
The diagnostic loop begins when contradiction exposes a shared presupposition and converts opposition into joint invalidity.
Critical removal of the completed object-domain returns cosmology as regulative inquiry rather than abolishing its demand.
The unconditioned is the dominant attractor because it directs inquiry while receding from every empirical attainment.
Possible experience and empirical lawfulness form a coupled attractor-gate that both licenses objectivity and filters admissible explanation.
Cosmical composition forms a representation loop in which regress constitutes world-totality while preventing its pregiven completion.
Division forms a decomposition loop producing infinite determinability without an actually completed stock of parts.
The mathematical-dynamical classifier routes conflict toward reciprocal rejection or qualified reconciliation.
Exposure produces a phase change from deception to vigilance, not escape from the totalizing impulse.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Conditioned appearance + categorial organization → selection of a regressively subordinated condition-series.
Serial regress + rational demand for completeness → transcendental idea of absolute totality.
Idea misread as determinable object + appearances converted into things in themselves → antinomial opposition.
Unadjudicable conflict → reflexive transcendental critique of the object-presupposition generating both sides.
Withdrawal of the shared self-subsistent world-model → joint invalidity of opposed predicates + preservation of empirical reality.
Dissolved constitutive totality → cosmological idea recoded as a regulative principle.
Regulative problem + classification by form of synthesis → differentiated modes of noncompletion.
Empirical composition → indefinite extension; continuous division → regress in infinitum; neither → completed infinite aggregate.
Homogeneous mathematical series → exclusion of an unconditioned member; heterogeneous dynamical series → conditional nonempirical ground preserving lawful regress.
Regulative continuation → systematic correction + renewed conditioning + no final cosmological closure.
Conditioned empirical synthesis → demand for unconditioned totality.
Serial-categorial selection → four cosmological problem-fields.
Objectification of totality → paired antinomial claims.
Unresolved conflict → diagnosis of how reason mistakes an idea for a valid object.
Transcendental ideality → dissolution of the completed world-object + retention of empirical inquiry.
Synthesis-sensitive classification → indefinite regress, infinite division, or conditionally admissible nonempirical grounding.
Regulative nonclosure → widened empirical correction + recurrent vigilance.
The world is reclassified from a total object into an open regressive order and horizon of possible synthesis.
Objectivity is separated from independent subsistence, making empirical realism compatible with transcendental ideality.
The legitimacy of a cosmological question must be assessed before its bivalent answers can be evaluated.
Finite and infinite cease to be exhaustive world-properties and become indices of premature closure.
Infinity is differentiated into indefinite empirical extension, infinite divisibility, and prohibited actual completion.
Contradiction is reclassified from an obstacle into a method for exposing invalid object-models.
The opposition between dogmatism and skepticism collapses into critical limitation that preserves inquiry.
Categories become visible as structurally dual: stable within experience and dialectical under absolute totalization.
Explanation is protected simultaneously from metaphysical closure and covert supersensible interruption.
Philosophical solution is reclassified from possession of an answer-object into reflexive determination of the representation producing the question.
Transcendental ideality becomes a diagnostic method rather than merely a static doctrine about appearances.
At the surface level, disputes over world magnitude, material composition, causality, dependence, temporal beginning, and spatial boundary supply exemplary conflict-material.
At the structural level, temporally successive synthesis interacts with reason’s demand for total conditions to produce regress and recurrent totalization.
At the metastrategic level, adjudication between doctrines is replaced by diagnosis of the shared premise and validity of the alleged object.
At the ontological and temporal level, reality consists of conditioned appearances synthesized successively without a knowable first, final, or total condition.
At the methodological and performative level, paired demonstrations enact reason’s self-reversal and convert apparent defeat into critical method.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Reason requires a complete conception of conditioned reality while the required regulative end remains structurally unavailable.
The regulative principle lacks constitutive object-status yet exerts force comparable to an axiom, leaving its precise operation underdetermined.
Intellectual termination is prohibited in empirical regress, yet a positive intelligible condition is required for dynamical reconciliation.
Possible experience is the criterion of speculative objectivity, but phenomenal inaccessibility cannot become ontological denial or theoretical disproof of practical orientation.
Procedural infinity must remain distinct from actual infinity, although the distinction between its forms is indispensable and unstable.
The system makes negative determinations concerning the world-whole while denying that the whole is an available object of determination.
The indirect confirmation of transcendental ideality risks circularity because the antinomial diagnosis presupposes the representational framework it confirms.
Critical limitation must count as positive resolution even though it cannot permanently extinguish the illusion requiring resolution.
A category mutates into a transcendental idea when conditioned synthesis is extended toward absolute completion.
Totality mutates from a world-property into a procedural question and regulative direction that determines no object.
Antinomy mutates from doctrinal deadlock into joint invalidity and then into a typed field with nonidentical resolutions.
The unconditioned mutates from an alleged terminus into an unattainable horizon and selective gate.
Infinity mutates from intrinsic magnitude into differentiated permissions and progressive determinability.
Skepticism mutates from oscillation and surrender into cathartic criticism of invalid question-formation.
Closure mutates from architectonic completion of the world into the positive completion of reason’s self-limitation.
The intelligible condition mutates from an illicit empirical terminus into a conditionally admissible nonmember of dynamical synthesis.
Reality is a lawful network of conditioned appearances, synthesis, and regress rather than a completed inventory of things.
The subject is a finite regressor inside experience that generates illusion and then acts as its tribunal.
Time is the asymmetrical medium of successive synthesis that requires antecedents while preventing their simultaneous total presence.
The unconditioned is a receding horizon and selective gate that orients movement without becoming an empirical destination.
Critical struggle consists in converting compulsive reification into navigation that preserves empirical continuity.
Escape from totalizing illusion is unavailable; the remaining agency is recurrent vigilance and situated correction.
The extracted axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the derivation of cosmological demand, objectification, antinomy, critical dissolution, synthesis-sensitive differentiation, and regulative return.
The exact mechanism of regulative use and the positive character of the intelligible dynamical condition remain underdetermined.
The architecture is coherent only if logical necessity, empirical availability, and ontological givenness remain non-equivalent.
The architecture is strongest in the sequence from reification through antinomial diagnosis to regulative reconstruction differentiated by synthesis.
Reconstruction depends on preserving staged reversal, recursive return, and synthesis-specific sequencing rather than reducing critique to static prohibition.
Individual proof assumptions, procedural infinity, and the intelligible condition remain resistant to complete axiomatic reduction.
Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if neither dogmatic side is selected and empirical inquiry survives the dissolution of cosmological objecthood.
