units.title: Chapters 10–12

items.text: The central problem is how the same natural operations can generate causal belief, prejudice, fictive ontology, and the procedures by which philosophy regulates them.
Repeated conjunction, relation, and facilitated transition form a common engine whose outputs differ less by origin than by the degree to which comparison and experiment control them.

At this scale the argument becomes a genealogical-methodological reconstruction: intrinsic substance and power are displaced by collections of qualities, observable relations, customary transitions, and regulated causal projections.
Reflection does not transcend natural belief; it exposes discrepancies within it and forces a bifurcation between fictive metaphysical repair and more extensive general rules.
Resemblance and ease of transition are epistemically neutral: uncontrolled, they produce prejudice and fictive unity; experimentally opposed by difference, they isolate causal circumstances.

Philosophical correction therefore consists in recursive circumstance-analysis, widened experience, and semantic restraint rather than access to necessary connection or an independent rational faculty.
The movement is spiral and mutation-driven: custom generates an inference, discrepancy reopens it, a higher-order rule reorganizes it, and the corrective result becomes subject to renewed testing.

Closure is operational but nonterminal: metaphysical inquiry into hidden substance or power ceases, while empirical causal judgment remains corrigible because neither custom nor circumstance-analysis admits final completion.
[Persistent] Repeated conjunction and close relation acquire cognitive efficacy by facilitating transitions among perceptions rather than by revealing intrinsic bonds among objects.
[Persistent] Neither substance nor causal power is available through mere inspection; actual causal judgment begins only from experienced relational structure.
[Mutating] Ease of mental transition produces belief when it transfers vivacity, but produces fictive identity and simplicity when its own fluency is attributed to objects.
[Persistent] Natural customary transition precedes reflection and remains active after reflective correction; philosophy can redirect but cannot abolish it.
[Mutating] Resemblance extends inference beyond identical cases, becoming prejudice when material differences are neglected and an experimental operator when resemblance is controlled by contrast.
[Emergent] Reflection works through comparison, counterinstance, and circumstance-variation; it corrects fluent apprehension by making suppressed differences operationally salient.
[Emergent] Philosophical normativity is immanent to custom: more extensive and constant regularities regulate narrower associations without invoking an extra-customary tribunal.
[Emergent] Actual causation is operationally constituted by contiguous, temporally ordered, uniform conjunction among experimentally discriminated circumstances.
[Persistent] Phenomena are compound, so causal identity must migrate from whole objects to qualities, differences, and auxiliary circumstances isolated through comparative tests.
[Mutating] Contradiction and disappointed expectation do not determine their own resolution: they can provoke fictive substrates, prejudicial persistence, or renewed experimental decomposition.

[Persistent] Evidential warrant and experienced conviction are separable because conviction varies with vivacity, transition, temporal distance, and presentation, while warrant depends on comparative regularity.
[Terminal] Corrective inquiry has no self-applying or final form: every metarule competes with prior habit, and every experiment becomes subject to renewed circumstance-analysis.
[Attractor] Legitimate explanation converges on two constraints: terms must possess assignable ideational content, and causal distinctions must survive discriminating variation.
[Attractor] Moderate scepticism suspends claims to hidden substance and power while preserving disciplined empirical inquiry into observable regularities.
[Stable Identity] Constant conjunction retains its function as the empirical condition of causal inference while remaining explicitly distinct from perceived necessary connection.

[Functional Recurrence] Facilitated transition recurs as belief-production, inferential compression, imputed identity, and imputed simplicity; its function changes with the object onto which fluency is projected.
[Mutation] Custom moves from a first-order producer of expectation and prejudice to the material from which second-order philosophical rules are constructed.
[Reversal] Resemblance changes from a source of illicit transfer into a controlled comparative instrument once difference is deliberately introduced.
[Migration] Reflective comparison migrates from exposing variation and composition in bodies to isolating causal circumstances within compound phenomena.
[Escalation] The general rule expands from a correction of prejudicial inference into a recursive methodology for causal projection, decomposition, and experimental enlargement.
[Displacement] Qualities cease to require a substantial bearer and become separable elements whose causal relevance must be experimentally determined.
[Terminal Transformation] Contradiction ceases to be evidence for an unknown substrate and becomes a demand to identify an omitted difference, scope condition, or auxiliary cause.
[Absorption] The local theory of vivacity is absorbed into the current-level distinction between psychological uptake and methodological warrant.
[Disappearance] Substance, substantial form, accident, faculty, and occult quality disappear after supplying negative cases of how unexplained transition is converted into simulated ontology.
[Lower-Layer Local] Temporal fading, historical transmission, sign generality, and passion-amplification remain local specifications of how belief-force varies.
[Lower-Layer Local] The individual comparative, proportional, and incomplete-cause rules remain local instruments; their recursive subjection to renewed variation scales upward.
[Lower-Layer Local] The specific genealogy of matter, substantial forms, accidents, and occult qualities remains a local historical diagnosis.
[Scaled] The denial of intrinsic causal legibility scales upward into a general restriction against both a priori causal ontology and metaphysical explanation by hidden powers.
[Bridge] The conflict between first-order and second-order general rules bridges the psychology of prejudice and the methodology of experimental causal judgment.
[Bridge] Smooth mental transition connects belief-formation to fictive object-construction, revealing a shared mechanism beneath epistemic and ontological error.
[Catalyst] Reflectively disclosed contradiction catalyzes the transition from passive customary association to either metaphysical repair or active experimental differentiation.
[Recoded] “Same cause” is recoded from identity of whole objects to identity of experimentally isolated operative circumstances.
[Superseded] Objective substances, intrinsic faculties, and occult agencies are superseded by relational descriptions that remain answerable to assignable ideas and observable variation.
[Current-Level Emergent] Genuine philosophy becomes the conjunction of psychological self-diagnosis, comparative experiment, and refusal of semantically empty closure.
Causal roles cannot be assigned by conceptual inspection or an a priori taxonomy of objects.
Identity, simplicity, cohesion, and causal agency cannot be grounded in an intelligible invariant substance.
No proposition possesses a belief-force invariant under temporal distance, mediation, presentation, and disposition.
Philosophical correction cannot appeal to a rational faculty independent of custom, imagination, comparison, and experience.
Ease, repetition, resemblance, and customary inseparability do not by themselves establish object identity, metaphysical dependence, or causal efficacy.
Technical vocabulary cannot acquire explanatory force through repetition, professional authority, or verbal resemblance alone.
Neither formal rules nor a decisive experiment can eliminate the need for renewed judgment and circumstance-analysis.
Reflection does not permanently suppress the customary propensity whose outputs it corrects.
Human affects, intentions, and inward agency cannot be projected into nature as explanations of external phenomena.
The system requires rationalist transparency to be false: causes, substances, and powers must not be intrinsically legible to conception.
It also excludes absolute irregularity and total kind-instability; without provisionally stable resemblances, causal uniformity and comparative projection would collapse.

Normative correction must not depend on an external tribunal, yet it must not reduce to whichever custom is psychologically strongest; the system survives only through comparative extension and constancy.
Object identity and causal identity cannot be primitively given; both must remain decomposable into qualities, relations, and operative circumstances.
Explanatory usefulness cannot legitimate an otherwise inconceivable posit; fictive reconciliation and verbal closure must remain distinguishable from explanation.
A temporally invariant, affectively insulated, and uniformly rational subject cannot be admitted because belief is produced as a variable event of force-transmission and habit.
Experimental competence cannot be exhausted by possession of explicit rules; decisive variation must remain dependent on judgment that the rules cannot independently generate.
The system is organized around the absent metaphysical interior of causation: repeated conjunction is available, but the power supposedly connecting cause and effect is not.
The unavailable possibility of a transcendent criterion gives correction its recursive form: philosophy can judge custom only through a more extensive organization of custom.
No final reconciliation between natural propensity and reflective discipline is available; their conflict is constitutive rather than temporary.
No terminal causal decomposition is admissible because every isolated circumstance can become part of a newly compounded phenomenon requiring further control.
The invariant bearer is absent on both sides of cognition: objects dissolve into related qualities, while subjects dissolve into temporally variable operations of habit, comparison, and force.
The system circles but cannot fully formalize the exact boundary between warranted generalization and prejudice; that boundary remains dependent on scope, constancy, and discriminating judgment.

Because prejudice, fictive ontology, and causal judgment arise from related customary mechanisms, causal method must be understood as a disciplined mutation of association rather than the intervention of a foreign faculty.
Resemblance has no stable epistemic valence: left unopposed, it exports vivacity and object-unity; paired with controlled difference, it isolates operative causal circumstances.
Contradiction is a methodological fork: imagination may conceal it through a substrate, preserve it through prejudice, or convert it into a test for omitted differences and auxiliary causes.
Causal uniformity functions as a regulative rule for organizing experience, not as evidence that necessary connection or productive power has become perceptible.

A methodologically warranted inference may remain psychologically faint, while an experimentally defective association may remain vivid; epistemic rank and subjective force therefore require separate assessment.
Correction is necessarily provisional because reflective metarules never erase first-order habit and experimental controls never escape renewed circumstance-analysis.

Once bodies are treated as collections of separable qualities, causal inquiry can no longer take whole substances as primitive causes; it must identify operative qualities within relational compounds.
Legitimate theoretical distinctions are constrained simultaneously by semantics and experiment: they must correspond to assignable ideas and support discriminating variations.

Moral inquiry is especially unstable because obscure variables interact with vivid signs, passions, and anthropomorphic projection, increasing both causal opacity and susceptibility to prejudicial inference.
Moderate scepticism does not terminate causal practice; it terminates the conversion of empirically useful rules into claims about hidden ontological powers.
Normativity is naturalized without being reduced to immediate habit: warranted judgment is the recursive stabilization of custom through broader comparison, counterinstance, and experimental control.
The resulting ontology is thin and relational: separable qualities enter recurring spatiotemporal conjunctions, but neither substantial bearers nor intrinsic productive powers are required.
The epistemic subject becomes a temporally variable relay among impressions, habits, comparisons, passions, and reflective rules rather than a stable faculty of rational assent.
Anomaly becomes productive only when it is prevented from hardening into fiction: disappointed expectation must trigger decomposition rather than occult supplementation.
Time is constitutive at two levels: causal order requires priority and succession, while belief-strength varies with recency, mediation, and the temporal mode of survey.
Evidence becomes two-dimensional: comparative regularity determines warrant, whereas vivacity and transitional facility determine experienced conviction and affective efficacy.
Method cannot be fully formalized because its rules generate tasks of discrimination whose decisive execution depends on non-algorithmic judgment and expanded experience.
Natural and moral phenomena occupy one causal field, but moral inquiry demands stronger safeguards because its operative circumstances are obscured by affective and imaginative participation.
Philosophical success consists not in recovering objective necessity but in keeping inference revisable, terms meaningful, and metaphysical demands from dictating fictive closure.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Repetition → custom → facilitated transition → vivified expectation → reinforced readiness for the same transition forms the basal belief loop.
Related qualities → fluent survey → imputed identity or simplicity → reflective contradiction → substance fiction → further metaphysical categories forms the ontological escalation loop.
Resemblance → first-order generalization → counterinstance → more general rule → continued competition with the first propensity forms the prejudice-correction loop.
Compound phenomenon → controlled variation → provisional circumstance-isolation → new compound description → renewed variation forms the experimental recursion.
Contradiction is the principal bifurcation point: one path proliferates fictive entities, while the other intensifies comparison and experimental differentiation.
“General rule” becomes a machine when it ceases merely to state regularity and begins selecting, condemning, and reorganizing lower-order transitions.
“Circumstance” becomes a machine when causal identity shifts from whole objects to variables that can be compared, removed, decomposed, or supplied as co-causes.
Moderate scepticism functions as an attractor that halts metaphysical proliferation without halting empirical recursion.

Apparent repetition marks phase change when customary recurrence is re-entered as an object of reflection: the same mechanism then becomes belief, error, diagnosis, or correction according to its recursive position.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Distinct qualities + repeated conjunction + close relation → facilitated transition among perceptions.
Facilitated transition + present force or fluent survey → causal expectation / imputed identity / imputed simplicity.
Temporal distance, contrary instance, analytic comparison, or changed circumstance → interrupted fluency → weakened conviction or disclosed contradiction.
Uncontrolled contradiction + retained demand for unity or agency → substance / occult quality / prejudicial persistence → simulated closure.
Controlled contradiction + counterinstance + broader comparison → second-order general rule → accidental–efficacious distinction.
Compound phenomenon + controlled resemblance and difference → operative circumstance / common quality / missing co-cause → provisional causal attribution.
Provisional attribution + renewed circumstance-analysis + enlarged experimental sphere → recursively corrected causal map.
Absence of intrinsic power + absence of final control → moderate sceptical restriction + continued empirical inquiry.
Variable vivacity and presentation → unequal psychological uptake of equally regulated conclusions → persistent gap between method and assent.
Repeated conjunction and related qualities → fluent customary transition.
Fluent transition → causal belief, resemblance-extension, and imputed object-unity.
Temporal, comparative, or experimental disruption → diminished conviction, disclosed composition, or failed expectation.
Disruption → bifurcation between fictive metaphysical repair and reflective reclassification.
Reflective reclassification → more general rules + controlled resemblance and difference → causal circumstance-isolation.
Circumstance-isolation → provisional projection → renewed experimental control → widened evidential field.
Recursive correction → rejection of hidden power and empty terminology → moderate sceptical, nonterminal closure.
Reason and error cease to belong to independent faculties; both become differently organized outputs of relation, custom, comparison, and rule-governed correction.
Ontology is divided into two registers: fictive intrinsic structure is genealogically dissolved, while observable relational structure remains available for causal practice.
Resemblance becomes a truth-neutral operator whose epistemic status depends on whether difference and counterinstance control its extension.
Contradiction is reclassified from a demand for an unseen bearer into a diagnostic opportunity for causal decomposition.
Causation becomes thinkable without intrinsic power: its legitimate content lies in regular succession, controlled comparison, and projection within tested kinds.
Evidence divides into logical-methodological warrant and psychological-affective force, dissolving the assumption that valid arguments must command proportionate conviction.
Philosophical vocabulary is judged by ideational content and experimental work rather than by systematic position or technical appearance.
Natural and moral phenomena enter a unified causal terrain, differentiated by variable opacity rather than by distinct causal architectures.
The hidden presuppositions of empirical inquiry become visible: stable kinds, discriminable circumstances, and nonbrute irregularity are required even after necessary connection is denied.
Surface level: the system addresses variations in belief, rules for judging causes, and the ancient categories of substance, form, accident, faculty, and occult quality.
Structural level: relation and repetition facilitate transitions; comparison and variation interrupt them; higher-order rules reorganize the resulting expectations and contradictions.
Metastrategic level: philosophy intervenes by redirecting custom, expanding the experimental field, and refusing fictive or verbal closure when objective connection is unavailable.

Ontological / Temporal level: reality is composed of separable qualities in temporally ordered conjunctions, while identity, conviction, and causal attribution vary with survey, succession, and experimental scope.
Methodological / Performative level: the architecture performs its thesis by repeatedly turning its own rules, categories, and conclusions into objects of further comparison and correction.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Custom supplies prejudice, causal belief, corrective metarules, and the criterion of greater regularity; the distinction between bad and good custom therefore remains immanent and incompletely secured.
The claim that causation depends wholly on constant conjunction remains strained by the additional requirements of contiguity and temporal priority.
Strict causal uniformity conflicts with contrary experience and graded probability unless every apparent exception is reassigned to an undiscovered difference or missing co-cause.
A priori causal openness coexists with dependence on stable kinds, clear experiments, and discriminable circumstances whose criteria are not fully specified.
Denial of observable necessary connection coexists with strong projection from a clear experiment, leaving the practical authority of uniformity stronger than its ontological basis.
A genealogy of substance explains why it is believed but does not alone establish its falsity; the refutation additionally depends on the absence of an assignable idea and the separability principle.
Experimentally isolated qualities risk becoming replacements for occult qualities unless their identity remains tied to reproducible comparison rather than verbal designation.
The architecture distinguishes warrant from conviction but supplies no quantitative rule connecting impression-strength, transitional facility, and resulting assent.
Resemblance mutates from spontaneous evidence into a controlled experimental variable when paired with discriminating difference.
The general rule mutates from a habitual extension that produces prejudice into a reflective metarule that regulates lower-order inference.
Contradiction mutates from a stimulus for ontological repair into an experimental demand for further differentiation.
Cause mutates from an apparently whole object into a common quality, differentiating circumstance, compound contribution, or auxiliary condition.
Sceptical cessation mutates from termination of the search for intrinsic power into the enabling boundary of continued empirical causal inquiry.
Reality is implicitly a field of separable qualities entering recurrent, contiguous, temporally ordered configurations without an observable inner power binding them.
The subject is a relay-system in which impressions, custom, imagination, comparison, passion, and reflective rules transfer, amplify, interrupt, and reorganize force.
Time is not a neutral container: causal priority, recency, gradual survey, distant comparison, and inferential mediation actively constitute both objects and beliefs.

The remaining struggle is between fluent closure and recursive differentiation; escape is not departure from custom but the controlled reopening of its products through variation, comparison, and sceptical restraint.
The global axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the cluster if facilitated transition, reflective disruption, and the bifurcation between fictive repair and experimental correction are preserved.
The architecture remains underdetermined at the points where it invokes more general rules, same kinds, clear experiments, adequate repetition, and essential circumstances.
The system is coherent at this scale as an immanent account of naturalized correction: the mechanisms generating error also supply the materials for disciplined judgment.
Its strongest architecture is the conversion of relation and custom into a branching machine capable of producing belief, prejudice, fictive ontology, and recursive causal method.
Reconstruction depends on recursive sequencing: natural transition must precede disruption, and disruption must precede either metaphysical proliferation or methodological control.
The architecture is weakest where anti-scholastic valuation, causal uniformity, and the superiority of sceptical cessation are asserted more strongly than their internal criteria determine.
Experimental sagacity and the variable force of conviction remain resistant to complete axiomatic reduction because neither decisive variation nor psychological intensity is rendered calculable.
Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if correction is not represented as abolishing imagination and scepticism is not represented as abolishing empirical inquiry.

units.title: Chapters 13–15

items.text: The central problem is how explanatory inquiry can remain operative after unknown substances, self-grounding reason, and unrestricted affective laws cease to provide legitimate foundations.

The system relocates explanation from hidden bearers and intrinsic powers to observable differences, experienced conjunctions, associative transitions, affective forces, and domain-specific thresholds.
Its argument becomes an immanent audit: concepts, faculties, and general laws are tested by their experiential origin, internal consequences, reciprocal applicability, and tendency to overgenerate.
The directional movement is universal claim → contradiction or excess → restrictive analysis → preservation of a limited mechanism rather than restoration of the original foundation.
Imagination is the common engine: it completes relations, confers vivacity, sustains belief, mediates passion, and produces error whenever its transitions outrun their conditions.
The self survives the destruction of substantial soul-talk not as an appearing bearer but as an operational object, comparator, and relatively durable pole of affective attribution.
Habit, custom, practice, and nature restore regular operation after metaphysical, epistemic, or causal certainty has been withdrawn, but they do not convert practical stability into truth.
Closure is recursive and pragmatic: inquiry continues through constrained natural propensity, repeatedly correcting both speculative excess and skeptical paralysis without reaching final foundation.
[Persistent] Legitimate explanation begins from experienced perceptions, conjunctions, pleasures, pains, and their observable transitions rather than from impression-transcendent entities.
[Emergent] Once unknown supports are excluded, the primary explanatory object becomes the network of relations and transformations among perceptions and affects.
[Attractor] Imagination is simultaneously the indispensable medium of cognitive and affective synthesis and the source of fictive completion, contradiction, and excess.
[Mutating] Relation is not a uniform binary bond: it changes across separability, spatial compatibility, causal succession, self-reference, comparison, publicity, and temporal durability.
[Persistent] Repetition becomes operational through habit or custom, which projects conjunctions, stabilizes classifications, and regularizes otherwise delicate transitions.
[Emergent] Cognitive and affective efficacy requires force: vivacity, pleasure, pain, passion, or propensity must animate a relation before it governs assent or self-evaluation.
[Persistent] Causal intelligibility does not require perceived necessity; experienced conjunction and the transition it induces provide the operative causal content.
[Persistent] Heterogeneous effects cannot be explained by indiscriminately extending one medium, faculty, or response-class over the entire field.

[Emergent] Unrestricted principles reveal their inadequacy by overgeneration: universal extension, pure reason, unrestricted fancy, and mere self-relation each produce contradictions or false positives.
[Mutating] Correction is immanent and restrictive: undecidability, skeptical diffidence, empirical practice, and threshold conditions limit mechanisms without abolishing them.
[Mutating] The self has no established status as a substantial bearer but remains indispensable as an object of passion and a temporally extended standard of comparison.

[Emergent] Natural production and representational success do not guarantee correspondence: belief may lack rational foundation, apparent location may be fictive, and self-estimation may diverge from welfare.
[Terminal] The viable endpoint is a reflexive science of human nature that investigates its own fallible operations under permanent skeptical and empirical restraint.
The demand for origin mutates from a semantic test excluding mental substance into a genealogy of belief and then into a distinction between primary affect and mediated self-directed passion.

Imagination reverses valence: first exposed as fabricating spatial conjunction, it becomes the necessary source of belief, then the associative medium whose affective operation must be gated rather than removed.
Relation migrates from logical separability and spatial compatibility into causal projection, comparative distinction, public discernibility, and temporal attachment.
Custom expands from projecting past conjunctions into future expectation to regulating philosophical assent and stabilizing passion, while retaining the capacity to exceed particular warrant.
The self is displaced from the role of hidden support into the role of represented object; substantial identity disappears while functional self-reference persists.

Contradiction changes function from a reciprocal weapon against material and immaterial systems into an endogenous conflict among natural faculties and finally into a diagnostic of affective overgeneration.

Causation is absorbed into a broader transition-model: constant conjunction licenses bodily influence on thought, habit converts conjunction into expectation, and affective conversion requires additional relational gates.
Limitation escalates from suspension of undecidable ontology, through skeptical restraint of cognition, to explicit restriction of a causal law by comparative, social, and temporal thresholds.
Spinozist retortion and immortality cease to be active objects after establishing two higher rules: privileged theories receive no exemption, and no simplicity claim yields necessary persistence.
The extended/nonspatial partition remains local as a spatial analysis, but its higher-order effect is the prohibition against explaining heterogeneous phenomena through one uniform medium.
Peculiarity, visibility, and durability remain local gates of pride and humility; what scales upward is the form of a threshold-dependent transformation rather than those particular thresholds.
Melancholy, diversion, social intercourse, and revived curiosity remain the local phenomenology of skeptical recovery; their scalable function is non-rational restoration of viable cognition.
Separability, contradictory natural beliefs, and the joy–pride distinction scale upward because each differentiates effects that an unrestricted theory falsely homogenizes.
Associative completion, customary projection, and general affective rules bridge the units by showing how repeated relations acquire force without becoming intrinsic necessities.
Definitional collapse, skeptical self-subversion, and affective overgeneration are transition catalysts: each forces a move from foundational or universal explanation to restricted operation.
The simple soul, autonomous understanding, and unconditional passion-law become obsolete as explanatory centers and are recoded as failed cases of unrestricted unification.

Matter–thought causation, the resumption of philosophy, and welfare’s divergence from self-estimation remain distinct local conclusions but jointly establish operation without metaphysical, epistemic, or affective equivalence.
No unknown substratum may be installed merely to support perceptions whose relations can be described without it.
No autonomous reason or external cognitive instrument can validate the faculties from outside the natural operations under examination.
Relation is neither an intrinsic, uniform, nor merely binary property; its force depends upon domain, competition, repetition, and mediation.
Imagination can neither be granted unrestricted authority nor eliminated, because both cognition and error arise through its operations.
Natural necessity, customary stability, and felt conviction do not establish truth, intrinsic value, or ontological homogeneity.
Neither universal extension, universal simplicity, pure understanding, nor mere self-relation can serve as an unrestricted explanatory principle.
No necessary alignment joins causal operation to substantial ontology, ordinary belief to certainty, or pride and humility to happiness and misery.
The architecture requires the falsity of the model in which appearances are accidents that become intelligible only by inhering in an independently knowable substance.
It requires the falsity of any epistemology in which reason can ground assent without habit, imagination, vivacity, passion, or natural propensity.
It excludes the model in which causation is intelligible only through resemblance, conceptual containment, or a perceived necessary nexus.
It excludes the model in which affective value transparently registers intrinsic good and evil independently of comparison, publicity, familiarity, and custom.
It disqualifies the assumption that failures at the margins can be ignored while a general law remains genuinely universal; edge cases determine the law’s required restriction.
It cannot admit a self that is simultaneously an inaccessible substance, a transparent foundation of cognition, and an invariant measure of personal worth.
The system is organized around the absence of an unmediated common medium joining spatial and nonspatial perception, belief and truth, or welfare and self-estimation.
The unavailable possibility is a standpoint from which substance, causation, cognition, and value could be validated together without using the fallible transitions under examination.
No perfect alignment is available between what is naturally produced and what is real: fictive location, unavoidable belief, and socially legible pride can each diverge from their objects.
Final repose is inadmissible: neither metaphysical certainty, permanent skepticism, nor perfectly calibrated customary judgment can terminate recursive correction.
The deepest absent object is a fully self-present subject that could bear perceptions, authorize reason, measure value, and guarantee its own persistence.

Once the bearer of perception and the intrinsic power of causation are withdrawn, the passion-system reveals the positive replacement: explanation becomes a study of gated transformations among experiential states.
Associative completion, habitual projection, and customary passion-rules are three scales of one operation by which relations acquire efficacy through repetition and mental transition.

Because imagination produces both indispensable cognition and systematic fiction, correction cannot purify thought of imagination; it must discriminate among imaginative operations by their conditions and consequences.

Reciprocal failure of materialism and immaterialism, failure of unrestricted fancy and pure understanding, and overproduction of pride instantiate one rule: explanatory extremes collapse when generalized beyond their proper domain.

The destruction of the substantial soul does not eliminate self-reference; it transforms the subject into a represented and temporally weighted node within causal, imaginative, and affective relations.
Time has no single function: habit projects future conjunction, anticipated loss weakens self-attribution, and conceivability prevents either matter or spirit from claiming necessary persistence.
Felt success cannot measure reality: apparent place may be fabricated, natural belief may remain unjustified, and intense self-evaluation may fail to register actual welfare.

Once theological privilege is removed and custom is recognized as behaviorally formative, speculative systems must be assessed partly by how their rules organize conduct rather than by claimed access to hidden reality.
Reality becomes operationally describable as a heterogeneous field of perceptions and affects linked by contingent, force-bearing transitions rather than unified by a known substratum.
The subject becomes an effect and target of organization: it is where memories, beliefs, comparisons, publicity, and durable attachments converge, not the substance from which they emanate.

Causal law is transformed into differential conversion: conjunction establishes possible transition, while domain-specific relations determine whether that transition becomes belief, apparent location, joy, pride, pain, or humility.
Temporality is naturalized as projection, anticipated loss, comparative duration, and conceivability of cessation; it supplies no proof of necessary identity or immortality.
Human agency is non-sovereign: assent and passion arise from propensities, habits, relations, and general rules that the will cannot simply suspend.
Epistemic normativity becomes regulatory rather than foundational: legitimate inquiry is the constrained use of unavoidable faculties, not their validation by an independent criterion.
Error is endogenous to successful machinery: the same operations that locate, project, classify, and stabilize also fabricate, contradict, and overextend.
The science of human nature must therefore operate experimentally and recursively, treating every generalization as a revisable mechanism whose limits are disclosed by its own excesses.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Causal or temporal association → imaginative relation-completion → apparent spatial placement → familiar attribution → renewed reinforcement of the fictive relation.
Repeated conjunction → habit → vivacity and expectation → ordinary action → further experienced conjunction forms the basic belief-production loop.
Valenced cause → candidate self-relation → comparative and social filtering → pride or humility → customary classification → facilitated future passion forms the affective loop.
Inquiry → skeptical intensification → affective paralysis → natural restoration → curiosity → renewed inquiry is the cluster’s explicit spiral rather than a linear resolution.
Universal mechanism → anomalous output → immanent critique → restrictive thresholds → preserved mechanism → renewed exposure to anomalies is the general escalation path.
Human nature is the principal attractor: disputes about soul, causation, certainty, and passion converge on the operations and limits of perception, imagination, habit, and affect.
“Relation” becomes a machine when it ceases to name a static connection and begins to regulate conceivability, spatial compatibility, causal expectation, self-reference, comparison, and passion.

“Custom” marks phase change rather than repetition: projection becomes cognitive stability, cognitive stability becomes methodological restraint, and restraint becomes affective regularization with renewed risk of excess.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Input field: heterogeneous perceptions, conjunctions, pleasures, pains, and candidate relations are given without an independently appearing support.
Semantic audit: demand experiential origin, distinguishability, and separability; exclude concepts that add no identifiable content.
Foundational subtraction: remove unknown substance, external necessary power, autonomous reason, and intrinsic affective scale.
Associative synthesis: conjunction and relation generate transition, while vivacity or valence supplies the force required for belief and passion.
Productive expansion: imagination completes relations, habit projects expectations, and self-reference converts primary affect into candidate self-evaluation.
Excess detection: fictive placement, contradictory beliefs, and indiscriminate pride expose the failure of unrestricted transition.
Restrictive gating: apply spatial compatibility, skeptical diffidence, practice, relational closeness, peculiarity, publicity, and duration.
Natural stabilization: habit, embodied restoration, and general rules produce workable regularity without guaranteeing truth or exact proportionality.
Recursive closure: submit stabilized operations to renewed audit; preserve empirically useful mechanisms while suspending metaphysical completion and global certainty.
Unknown support and unrestricted law → demand for experiential and operational justification.
Justificatory demand → decomposition into heterogeneous perceptions, conjunctions, pleasures, pains, and relations.
Decomposition → displacement of substance, intrinsic power, and pure reason by associative transition.
Associative transition → belief, apparent placement, and candidate self-directed passion.
Unrestricted transition → spatial fiction, contradictory natural belief, and affective overgeneration.
Contradiction and excess → reciprocal critique, skeptical restraint, and relational, comparative, social, and temporal gating.
Gated mechanism → customary and natural stabilization → constrained science of human nature → renewed skeptical audit.
The substance–accident map is replaced by a field of separable perceptions and describable transitions.
The mind–matter opposition is subordinated to cross-cutting differences among extended, nonspatial, cognitive, hedonic, and self-directed states.
Reason and imagination cease to be autonomous opposites; reason becomes a regulated operation within the imaginative and affective economy of assent.
Causation is detached from substantial ontology and redrawn as conjunction plus a domain-specific transition whose success may require additional gates.
The self is reclassified from hidden bearer to operational target of memory, comparison, publicity, and temporally durable attribution.
Value is divided into experienced good or evil, social legibility, self-estimation, and welfare; these distributions need not coincide.
Error is relocated from an alien disturbance to the overextension of otherwise necessary mechanisms such as imagination, habit, and custom.
Skepticism is redrawn from terminal suspension into a recurring control function that restrains both philosophical conviction and philosophical doubt.
General theories become readable as transformation models whose validity depends on specified ranges, thresholds, and failure conditions rather than maximal universality.
Surface level — The explicit objects are the soul’s substance, the grounds of belief and philosophy, and the conditions under which pleasure and pain become pride and humility.
Structural level — Heterogeneous inputs are joined by imagination, habit, causal transition, self-relation, comparison, and custom, then restricted where those operations overgenerate.
Metastrategic level — Inquiry advances by applying identical standards to privileged and rival systems, forcing universal claims to disclose their exclusions and limiting conditions.

Ontological/Temporal level — Reality contains spatially heterogeneous states; future and continuity are habitually projected; durable self-relations are stronger than transient ones; necessary persistence remains unavailable.

Methodological/Performative level — The system performs its thesis by generating speculative excess, exposing collapse, undergoing skeptical interruption, and returning with narrower, provisional machinery.
Social/Affective level — Public discernibility, comparison, custom, superstition, and philosophy show that representations acquire force through collective circulation and behavioral consequence.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The substantial self is excluded, yet a relatively durable self remains necessary as the object and comparator of passion; the status of this operational continuity is not fully specified.
No Archimedean criterion validates cognition, yet practice, experience, moderation, and critical examination are assigned regulatory authority without a complete account of their title.
Constant conjunction licenses actual matter–thought causation, but the available covariation does not fully individuate the cause or exclude competing conjunctions.
Imagination is both the condition of cognition and the source of contradiction; no wholly independent faculty exists to delimit its legitimate operations.
Familiarity depreciates value while custom stabilizes and may amplify passion; the architecture supplies no general priority rule when these effects conflict.
Nature restores belief and action without vindicating them, leaving practical necessity structurally separated from epistemic legitimacy.
Substance mutates from a proposed bearer into an excluded surplus, transferring explanatory burden to relations among perceptions.
Imagination mutates from local fabricator of place into the general medium of belief, memory, causal expectation, and affective association.
Relation mutates from logical and spatial compatibility into a graded force governing social distinction and temporal self-attachment.
The self mutates from a metaphysical candidate into a functional object that organizes attention, comparison, and passion without appearing as a separate impression.
Skepticism mutates from threatened cessation of inquiry into recurrent diffidence that enables rather than terminates constrained philosophy.
Universal law mutates into gated mechanism: failures no longer simply refute causal regularity but determine its range and internal conditions.
Custom mutates from a projector of expectation into a regulator of inquiry and passion, then reverses into a source of renewed overextension.
Reality appears as a field of unsupported, heterogeneous events linked by associative, habitual, causal, affective, social, and temporal relays.
The subject is a mobile junction within that field: a point at which vivacity becomes belief and valenced relations become self-attribution, not a hidden substance beneath them.
Time is a machine of projection and attenuation: repetition opens the future, anticipated loss weakens attachment, and possible annihilation prevents duration from becoming necessity.

No escape outside human faculties is available; viable navigation consists in moving between imaginative overproduction and skeptical paralysis through experience, custom, social practice, and recurrent correction.

The extracted axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the cluster if perception-first analysis, associative mediation, heterogeneous effects, threshold restriction, customary stabilization, and skeptical recursion are retained together.

The architecture remains underdetermined regarding the external status of matter, causal individuation, the normative authority of lively reason, exact affective thresholds, and the scope of general rules.
The system is coherent at this scale as a recursive operational architecture, not as a deductive foundation or final reconciliation of its natural conflicts.
Its strongest architecture is the conversion of failed ontological foundations into a science of constrained transitions whose errors arise from the excess of their own productive mechanisms.

Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if negation is followed by operational return: conceptual invalidation must lead to empirical causation, skepticism to natural restoration, and overgeneration to restriction.

The indispensable residue resistant to complete axiomatic reduction is differential felt force—vivacity, pleasure, pain, propensity, familiarity, and passion—because these intensities make transitions operative but are not derivable from relation alone.

units.title: Chapters 16–18

items.text: The central problem is how socially directed passions vary while their represented objects, qualities, or conditions remain unchanged.

The governing thesis is that social affect is generated by relation-conditioned movements of vivacity: others affect the self through sympathetic reproduction or construction, and through comparison that alters apparent self-position.
The argument becomes a distributed causal reconstruction in which anomalies eliminate original instincts, intrinsic values, and rational-interest models in favor of associative mechanisms.
The self functions first as a source of vivacity, then as recipient of communicated sentiment, and finally as the comparative term whose apparent condition is altered by another’s fortune.
Sympathy carries or constructs another’s satisfaction, esteem, contempt, or sorrow within the observer, producing reputation, affection, wealth-esteem, utility-pleasure, and pity.
Comparison preserves one affect across transition to another object, reverses its contribution to self-estimation, and generates envy or malice without requiring injury or autonomous malevolence.
Generated passions recursively modify their own conditions through justificatory judgment, imagined self-attribution, reflected esteem, and attempts to alter or sever comparative relations.
Closure is conditional rather than quantitative: a common relational architecture is established, but the thresholds governing conversion, comparison, and mode selection remain unspecified.
[Persistent] Ideas and impressions differ principally in force and vivacity, permitting associative processes to transform represented affect into operative passion without changing its content.
[Persistent] Relations are effective only as directed pathways that facilitate, preserve, intensify, interrupt, or redirect imaginative transition.
[Persistent] Social passion requires a coupling between affective force and a relation that assigns or compares that force to a person.
[Mutating] The self is not a sovereign source of valuation: its initial vivacity enables the very transitions through which external sentiments and comparative conditions alter it.
[Mutating] Sympathy begins as conversion of an inferred sentiment into an impression but expands into constructive simulation capable of supplementing or replacing the source’s actual emotion.

[Emergent] Sympathy and comparison are distinct transformations of retained affect: sympathy imports another’s represented condition, whereas comparison converts that condition into an inverse estimate of the self.
[Emergent] Affective valence belongs neither to representation nor object alone; it depends on whether the object is directly surveyed, sympathetically appropriated, or comparatively opposed.

[Mutating] Personal attribution is regulated by forms of certification—durability, intention, authority, causal inference, and general expectation—that determine whether an affect is attached to a person and sustained.
[Emergent] Relational proximity is valence-neutral amplification: it can intensify affection, praise, pity, rivalry, envy, or humiliation according to the process routed through it.

[Attractor] Social affect has a topology in which authority, resemblance, contiguity, acquaintance, convergence, direction, and separation govern force more decisively than bare content or absolute rank.
[Attractor] The recurrent generative circuit is self → related other → transformed affect → altered self, with the altered self producing further judgments, signs, desires, and reflected sentiments.
[Terminal] Passions can endogenously produce the beliefs and imagined conditions that preserve or amplify them.
[Terminal] No intrinsic affective baseline stabilizes self-worth, social value, or hierarchy independently of transmitted sentiment and active comparison.
[Stable identity] Force and vivacity retain their function as the common currency linking ideas, impressions, associative transitions, and passions.
[Functional recurrence] Relation recurs as a conductor of sympathy, a condition of durable affection, a bidirectional pathway of attachment, and a gate permitting comparative impressions to interact.
[Mutation] Sympathy shifts from reproducing another’s expressed sentiment to appropriating proprietary satisfaction and finally to constructing sorrow absent from the observed person.
[Domain migration] Resemblance moves from general human access to other minds, through affection and pity, into the wider topology determining which persons become affectively comparable.
[Mutation] The self moves from vivid associative origin, to object of socially communicated judgment, to variable magnitude constituted against related others.

[Reversal] Pleasure and pain cease to have invariant direction: another’s satisfaction can become esteem through sympathy or pain through comparison, while another’s misery can become pity or malicious pleasure.
[Reversal] Proximity changes from a means of sympathetic intimacy into a condition of intensified rivalry without ceasing to perform its basic function of preserving affect across transition.
[Escalation] General rules progress from tests of causal regularity to constructive templates that supply absent passions and project altered emotional magnitude back onto objects.
[Absorption] Intention and evaluator authority lose the status of isolated causes and become forms of personal certification governing durable attribution and evidential uptake.

[Terminal transformation] Esteem becomes recursive social capital: communicated satisfaction generates esteem, perceived esteem increases satisfaction, and renewed satisfaction generates further esteem.

[Disappearance] Original fame, intrinsic wealth-value, calculated advantage, and autonomous malevolence disappear after their explanatory roles are redistributed across sympathy, comparison, and associative topology.

[Lower-layer local] The exact weighting of evaluator authority, self-concurrence, jest, and numerical accumulation remains specific to reputational influence rather than defining every social passion.

[Lower-layer local] The distinction between durable qualities and transient intentional actions solves the temporal attribution of love and hatred but scales upward only as a general certification principle.
[Lower-layer local] The contingent conjunction of love with benevolence and hatred with anger remains an irreducible constitutional supplement rather than a global relational mechanism.
[Lower-layer local] Habitual projection from altered emotion to altered object-magnitude is the specific perceptual machinery of comparative judgment, not the general form of sympathy.
[Scales upward] Force, vivacity, associative transition, and retained impressions form the common machinery through which all three units generate social affect.
[Bridge] Fame and wealth-esteem jointly establish that social rank is produced by circulated satisfaction and reflected judgment rather than by isolated possession or intrinsic excellence.
[Bridge] Pity and envy demonstrate that proximity does not determine valence; it intensifies whichever sympathetic or comparative operation controls the transition.
[Catalyst] Constructed pity, resisted contempt, and direct pain joined to comparative pleasure force the separation of affective reception from belief, source-fidelity, and direct valence.
[Superseded] Primitive social appetites and static classifications are recoded as outputs of directed transitions, relational weights, and recursive feedback.
Social passions are not independent instincts responding uniformly to praise, wealth, misery, enjoyment, or rank.
Social value is not fixed by intrinsic merit, objective magnitude, sensible form, or absolute inequality.
Relations are not inert, symmetric classifications; their force depends on direction, convergence, continuity, and the transitions they enable.
Invariant representation does not guarantee invariant judgment or affective response.
Sympathy is neither immediate access to another mind nor necessarily faithful reproduction of another’s actual passion.
Rational judgment, calculated advantage, and objective justice are not sufficient sovereign causes of social affection.

A passion is not identical with its ordinary practical tendency: love need not conceptually contain benevolence, hatred need not contain anger, and misery need not remain an object of pain under comparison.
The cluster requires the falsity of an autonomous self whose valuation can remain insulated from communicated sentiments and comparable others.
It excludes a neutral tribunal capable of judging worth independently of prior passion, associative vivacity, and reflected social affect.
It disqualifies any model in which stable representation fixes stable judgment regardless of affective sequence and route.
It cannot admit transparent one-to-one correspondence between another’s interior state and the observer’s sympathetic impression.

It rules out purely linear causality because passion can generate its own judgments, esteem can amplify the satisfaction it reflects, and comparative pain can motivate alteration of its relational cause.
Objective hierarchy cannot be affectively operative without an associative route that makes persons proximate, authoritative, familiar, or comparable.
Ideas and impressions cannot be absolutely different kinds, because the entire social-affective architecture requires conversion by altered vivacity.
No necessary moral order may guarantee that relational intensification produces benevolence rather than rivalry, pity rather than malice, or esteem rather than mortification.
The deepest absent object is an intrinsic baseline of self-worth against which social communication and comparison could be finally corrected.
The system lacks a general criterion determining when another’s condition will be directly surveyed, sympathetically appropriated, or comparatively inverted.
No independent metric fixes the threshold at which relation transfers enough vivacity, sustains comparison, or converts an idea into an impression.
The authentic interior state of the other is unavailable as a final ground because social affect depends on inferred, reflected, supplemented, or fabricated sentiments.
A morally guaranteed direction for social relation is inadmissible: the same relational machinery can sustain affection, pity, esteem, envy, humiliation, or malice.
There is no affective position wholly outside the relational system from which its generated values could be judged without participating in their production.

Sympathy and comparison form dual operators on socially represented affect: the first reproduces or constructs another’s sentiment in the self, while the second preserves that sentiment as a contrasting force against the self.
Relational topology determines not only affective intensity but whether two personal conditions can interact at all.
Proximity is structurally ambivalent: it intensifies affection and pity when transition supports sympathetic appropriation, but intensifies envy when transition sustains comparative opposition.
Authority, intention, acquaintance, and general expectation are heterogeneous certification devices that stabilize otherwise transient affective attributions.
Fame and wealth operate through the same recursive status circuit: perceived satisfaction or approval generates esteem, and reflected esteem intensifies the state that elicited it.
Once sympathy can construct absent emotion, social effects depend on the observer’s operative model of another’s condition rather than on veridical access to that condition.
Another’s misery can simultaneously support direct sympathetic pain and comparative pleasure, so interpersonal affect need not resolve into a single valence.
Passion preserves itself through cognitive and imaginative supplementation: hatred generates injury judgments, while praise can generate a provisional self-attribution that makes praise effective.
Relational severance is a general affective strategy: concealment weakens shame, competing transitions weaken attachment, and distance disables envy without changing the underlying condition.
Fame, wealth-esteem, pity, envy, and malice require no autonomous faculty when their functions can be distributed among vivacity transfer, construction, contrast, and recursive self-estimation.
Social reality becomes a distributed affective computation in which persons continuously transmit, simulate, compare, and reflect one another’s conditions.
The subject becomes a relay and comparator rather than an enclosed origin: its vivid self-impression enables external affect to return as altered self-affection.
Value is generated in circulation: qualities, possessions, utility, rank, happiness, and misery acquire force through the paths by which their attendant sentiments reach or oppose the self.

Social hierarchy is recursively produced rather than merely perceived, because esteem amplifies satisfaction and comparative attention makes relationally proximate differences more affectively real than remote inequalities.
Social time is retentive and recursive: durable character sustains attribution, prior impressions remain active during transition, and lost comparative advantage becomes a new present pain.
Social judgment is epistemically endogenous to passion: testimony can alter self-belief, while prior passion can generate the judgment needed to preserve itself.
Strategic intervention shifts from changing objects to changing relational routes: authority can be discredited, identities concealed, associations severed, and comparative proximity weakened.
No ethical valence inheres in social connectedness itself; intensified relation can produce solidarity or antagonism according to the transformation governing retained affect.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Reputation loop: vivid self → inferred external judgment → sympathetic reproduction → pride or humility → increased receptivity to confirming judgments.
Wealth loop: possession → proprietary satisfaction → sympathetic esteem → perceived esteem → vanity → renewed satisfaction and esteem.
Injury loop: painful event → hatred → threatened diminution by justice or innocence → generated judgment of injury → stabilized hatred.

Envy escalation: comparative advantage → rival approach → loss of former comparative pleasure → comparison with the former state → new positive pain → pressure to sever relation or remove superiority.

Constructive-sympathy loop: observed condition → customary expectation of passion → construction of absent sentiment → intensified response through proximity or contrast → confirmation of the general expectation.
Relational intensification spirals rather than advances linearly: increased acquaintance or resemblance strengthens transition, which strengthens passion, which gives further force to related ideas.
The principal attractor is relation-mediated vivacity: heterogeneous passions repeatedly return to the question of which transition preserves, transfers, constructs, or opposes affective force.
The terminal escalation path is sign or condition → lively idea → impression → passion → judgment or desire → altered social condition → new sign or comparison.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Initialize a persistently vivid self S, represented persons O, attendant affects E(O), and a directed relational network R.
Weight R by resemblance, contiguity, acquaintance, kinship, authority, convergence, directionality, durability, and separation.
Direct attribution operator: pleasure or pain × durable quality or intention-sign × person-relation → stable love or hatred; strong affect × weak attribution → acute but unstable passion.
Sympathetic operator Sᵧ: signs or represented conditions → idea of another’s sentiment → relational vivacity transfer → corresponding or constructed impression in the observer.
Comparative operator C: R(O₁,O₂) → preservation of E(O₁) during transition → contrast with E(O₂) → altered apparent magnitude or self-condition.
Route Sᵧ through favorable or unfavorable evaluation to generate pride or humility; route it through satisfaction, utility, or misfortune to generate esteem, beauty, or pity.
Route C through another’s enjoyment to generate diminished self-estimation and envy; route it through anticipated misery to generate comparative elevation and malice.
Feed generated passion back into cognition and relation: passion strengthens associated ideas, constructs supporting judgments, reflects esteem, or seeks to alter the comparative field.

Attenuate output by disesteem, nonconcurrence, weak return transition, divided relations, distance, or conceptual separation; intensify it by authority, proximity, convergence, custom, and retained impression.
Closure rule: apparent exceptions do not trigger new faculties until variation in routing, certification, retention, construction, or comparison has been exhausted.
Unequal praise, unstable affection, anomalous pity, and unprovoked malevolence expose failures of undifferentiated social-passion models →
Original instinct, intrinsic value, rational advantage, moral injury, and autonomous malevolence are eliminated as sufficient causes →
Force and vivacity establish a common currency connecting representation, impression, and passion →
Directed relations establish the pathways, weights, continuities, and interruptions of affective transition →
Sympathy imports or constructs another’s sentiment, while comparison preserves and inverts its contribution to self-estimation →
The dual operations differentiate reputation, attachment, esteem, pity, envy, and malice without assigning each an independent faculty →
Generated passions recursively stabilize themselves through judgments, reflected esteem, imaginative supplementation, and relational intervention →
The system closes on a relational social ontology whose governing mechanisms are reconstructible but whose activation thresholds and mode-selection rules remain open.
Social passions are reclassified from discrete faculties into outputs of a shared relational economy of vivacity, retention, simulation, and contrast.
Relations become causal infrastructure rather than descriptive predicates: their direction and arrangement determine which affects can interact.
Other minds are reclassified as inferred and constructible affective models rather than transparent sources or sealed interiors.
The opposition between direct and social value collapses: social value is generated either by vicarious participation in another’s satisfaction or by inverse comparison with another’s condition.
Hierarchy is redrawn through affective adjacency: near rivals and credible judges can exert more force than objectively superior but relationally remote persons.
Agency becomes distributed across author, observer, relation, prior passion, general rule, and reflected response rather than residing solely in intentional action.
Distance, anonymity, concealment, and conceptual separation become active techniques for modifying passion without altering objective conditions.
Interpretation must distinguish content from force, relation from transition, direct valence from comparative valence, and transmitted emotion from constructed emotion.
Surface level: praise, blame, affection, anger, wealth-esteem, pity, envy, and malice present variable responses to persons and their fortunes.
Structural level: force and vivacity, directed relation, retained impression, sympathetic conversion, constructive simulation, and comparison generate those variations.
Metastrategic level: intervention targets authority, proximity, concurrence, associative continuity, and comparative framing rather than objective conditions alone.

Ontological/Temporal level: reality consists affectively of ideas and impressions differentiated by degree, while social time operates through persistence, succession, retention, recurrence, and reflected amplification.

Methodological/Performative level: the system repeatedly converts anomalies into controlled variations, tests rival causes, and returns apparent exceptions to a progressively enlarged relational mechanism.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Sympathy oscillates between reproduction and construction: the system requires causal signs for reputational transmission but permits pity to arise where the source passion is absent.
Proximity explains both agreeable affection and painful envy, but no general principle specifies what selects sympathetic identification rather than comparative opposition.
Direct and comparative valence can reverse one another, yet the activation rule deciding between direct survey and comparison remains underdetermined.
Relation is repeatedly established as necessary or contributory, but its sufficiency and quantitative threshold are never independently determined.
Reason functions both as evidential certification and as a product distorted or recruited by passion, leaving its independent corrective power unstable.
The shared relational machinery does not fully derive practical direction because the conjunction of love with benevolence and hatred with anger remains constitutionally posited.
The idea–impression threshold is the first mutation point: unchanged representational content becomes causally operative passion through increased vivacity.
Sympathy mutates from transmission into simulation when a represented condition and general rule generate an emotion not present in the observed person.
The self mutates from associative source into socially produced magnitude when another’s fortune becomes an inverse measure of its apparent condition.
Esteem mutates from communicated pleasure into a recursive status mechanism once the possessor perceives and reflects the observer’s response.
Relation mutates from resemblance or contiguity as static categories into a directional topology of outward passage, return, convergence, obstruction, and severance.
Direct affect mutates into comparative affect when a preceding impression is preserved and contributes inversely to the succeeding estimate.
Reality appears as a directed affective network whose nodes are persons and conditions, whose edges conduct vivacity, and whose feedback alters the nodes that initiated transmission.
The subject is a vivid but permeable relay: it receives signs, simulates other minds, compares positions, and returns the resulting passion as judgment, esteem, injury, or desire.
Time is a circuit of retained affect: past impressions persist into present transitions, durable attribution extends passions, and reflected consequences become new causes.

Available struggle consists in routing and rerouting affect—strengthening authority or resemblance, contesting attribution, breaking association, concealing identity, or altering comparative distance.
The cluster is reconstructible from force and vivacity, directed relation, personal certification, sympathetic transformation, comparative transformation, and recursive feedback.
These axioms preserve the actual movement only if sympathy and comparison remain distinct operations rather than being flattened into generic social influence.
The architecture is strongest where identical objects or conditions produce divergent effects under controlled changes in authority, intention, proximity, and comparative framing.
Coherence depends on accepting force and vivacity as the common currency and relations as causal pathways rather than static properties.
The principal underdetermination concerns mode selection and measure: the system does not specify when sympathy, direct survey, or comparison dominates, nor how much relation is sufficient.
Reconstruction depends on recursive sequencing because passion-generated judgment, reflected esteem, and remembered comparative advantage cannot be reduced to a static inventory of causes.

The indispensable residue resistant to full axiomatic reduction is the constitutional direction of compound passions and the unspecified thresholds governing idea–impression conversion and relational activation.
