units.title: Das Unbehagen in der Kultur (1930) · OCR review

items.text: Das System untersucht, warum Kultur zugleich unverzichtbarer Schutz gegen Hilflosigkeit, Naturgewalt und menschliche Aggression sowie eine eigenständige Quelle von Versagung, Schuld und Unglück ist.

Die globale These lautet, dass psychische und kulturelle Ordnungen Triebkräfte nicht beseitigen, sondern durch Grenzbildung, Bindung, Einschränkung, Verlagerung und Verinnerlichung so umverteilen, dass jede Stabilisierung neue Kosten erzeugt.

Das Argument wird zu einer genetischen, funktionalen und metapsychologischen Rekonstruktion, die religiöse Gewissheit, Glücksanspruch, Kulturideal und moralische Schuld von ihrer Selbstbeglaubigung trennt und auf ihre psychischen Operationen zurückführt.

Die Bewegung führt von psychischer Hilflosigkeit und Schutzsehnsucht über das unerfüllbare Glücksprogramm zur Kultur als Triebökonomie, von dort zur ursprünglichen Aggression und schließlich zur inneren Strafgewalt des Über-Ichs.
Diese Bewegung ist rekursiv und eskalatorisch, weil Schutz Abhängigkeit, Bindung Verzicht, Aggressionshemmung Innenwendung und Gewissensgehorsam zusätzliche Gewissensstrenge hervorbringt.

Individuelle Psyche, soziale Institution und Kulturgeschichte bilden keine getrennten Bereiche, sondern verschiedene Maßstäbe einer einzigen Umleitungsarchitektur, deren Skalierung Funktionen bewahrt, Ziele jedoch verschiebt.

Technischer Fortschritt schließt diese Architektur nicht, sondern verschärft sie, weil wachsende Verfügungsmacht weder Glück garantiert noch mit einer proportionalen Steigerung kultureller Aggressionsbindung verbunden ist.

Die Schließung bleibt offen und diagnostisch: Eine endgültige Versöhnung von Lust, Freiheit, Sicherheit, kultureller Einheit, Eros und Destruktion ist ausgeschlossen, während der Ausgang ihres Konflikts unentscheidbar bleibt.
[Persistent] Subjektive Intensität, kollektive Zustimmung, moralische Geltung und behauptete Zweckmäßigkeit legitimieren keinen Inhalt ohne genetische, funktionale und ökonomische Rekonstruktion.

[Persistent] Das Subjekt ist kein souveräner Ursprung, sondern ein geschichteter Umschlagpunkt körperlicher Bedürfnisse, libidinöser Besetzungen, destruktiver Richtungen, äußerer Autorität und internalisierter Forderungen.
[Persistent] Kultur sichert größere Gemeinschaften durch Schutz, Recht, Bindung und Triebeinschränkung, produziert jedoch gerade durch diese Integrationsmittel eigene Formen des Leidens.

[Emergent] Jede psychische oder kulturelle Schutzleistung ist eine Umverteilung begrenzter Befriedigung, Bindung und Aggression; sie kann Gefahren vermindern, ohne Abhängigkeit oder Triebkosten aufzuheben.

[Terminal] Das vom Lustprinzip gesetzte Glücksprogramm ist weder dauerhaft noch universell erfüllbar, und kultureller Fortschritt kann seine Unerfüllbarkeit nicht in eine gesicherte Versöhnung überführen.

[Mutating] Liebe mutiert von exklusiver Objekt- und Familienbindung über zielgehemmte Sozialbindung zum Erosprinzip kultureller Einheitsbildung, wobei jede Erweiterung ihre intensiven Ausgangsformen beschneiden muss.

[Mutating] Aggression eskaliert von zwischenmenschlicher Feindseligkeit zur Erscheinungsform des Todestriebs, wird kulturell nach außen oder innen umgelenkt und durch technische Macht bis zur möglichen Selbstvernichtung potenziert.
[Mutating] Grenzbildung mutiert von der psychischen Unterscheidung zwischen Selbst und Außen über Recht und Triebeinschränkung zur internalisierten Autorität des Über-Ichs.
[Attractor] Triebverzicht wird nach der Verinnerlichung von Autorität zum rekursiven Schuldverstärker, weil jeder neue Verzicht weitere Aggression an die Instanz überträgt, die ihn fordert.

[Attractor] Kulturgeschichte ist die unabschließbare Austragung des Konflikts zwischen einheitsbildendem Eros und bindungslösender Destruktion auf psychischen, institutionellen und menschheitsgeschichtlichen Maßstäben.

[Emergent] Kulturelle Zeit ist nichtteleologisch und rekursiv: Frühere Formationen bleiben unter funktionaler Mutation wirksam, während ungelöste Aggression, Schuld und technische Reichweite akkumulieren.

[Terminal] Technische Naturbeherrschung steigert Handlungsmacht ohne proportionale psychische Selbstbindung; deshalb endet die Architektur in einem offenen Überlebenskonflikt, nicht in einer Fortschrittsgarantie.

Religion kehrt nicht als eigenständiger Endgegenstand wieder, sondern wird nach ihrer psychogenetischen Umdeutung in die allgemeinere Architektur von Hilflosigkeit, Schutzabhängigkeit und Autoritätsbindung absorbiert.
Die Ichgrenze wandert aus der Individualgenese in Recht und soziale Einschränkung und kehrt schließlich als psychische Innengrenze zwischen Ich und Über-Ich zurück.
Glück verschiebt sich vom vermeintlichen Lebenszweck zur episodischen Befriedigung und danach zum negativen Bilanzposten kultureller Integration und technischer Risikosteigerung.

Liebe behält ihre bindende Funktion, erweitert aber ihren Geltungsbereich von exklusiver Nähe über umverteilte Libido bis zum überindividuellen Eros, der kulturelle Einheit erzeugt und dadurch zusätzliche Einschränkung verlangt.

Aggression bewahrt ihre energetische Identität, mutiert jedoch ontologisch und topisch von äußerer Feindseligkeit über Todestrieb und innere Strafgewalt zur technisch verstärkten Selbstvernichtungsmacht.
Einschränkung eskaliert von Realitätsanpassung und Rechtsbindung über Sexual- und Aggressionshemmung zur kausalen Umkehr, in der vollzogener Verzicht die ihn fordernde Gewissensinstanz verstärkt.

Autorität wechselt ihren Ort von äußerer Schutz- und Strafmacht zum individuellen Über-Ich und zum Kultur-Über-Ich; Moral verliert dabei ihre natürliche Valenz und wird zur Technik der Triebverwaltung.
Fortschritt kehrt mit umgekehrter Valenz wieder: Was zunächst Verfügung und Schutz steigert, wird schließlich zum Multiplikator jener Aggression, deren kulturelle Bindung nicht entsprechend wächst.

Das tatsächliche Vorkommen und die genaue Genese des ozeanischen Gefühls bleiben lokal; auf Gesamtbuchebene skaliert nur die methodische Trennung von Erlebnisintensität, Herkunft, Funktion und Wahrheitsgeltung.

Einzelne Glückstechniken und Kulturmerkmale verbleiben als lokale Typologien; global trägt allein die Regel, dass jede Technik eine besondere Verteilung von Entlastung, Abhängigkeit und Kosten erzeugt.

Organische Ursprungsspekulationen und die Urvatertötung bleiben genealogische Gerüste der unteren Ebene; nach oben skaliert die Verbindung von Ambivalenz, Identifizierung, Aggression und institutionalisierter Einschränkung.

Monogamie, Heterosexualität und Eigentumsordnung bleiben konkrete Norm- oder Testfälle; global relevant ist die Differenz zwischen historisch veränderlichen Aggressionskanälen und nicht auf Institutionen reduzierbarer Triebkonstitution.
Sadismus, Masochismus und klinische Symptomaufteilungen bleiben lokale Begründungsmittel; auf Gesamtbuchebene skaliert die indirekte Erschließung gemischter Triebkräfte und gehemmter Aggression.

Die technologische Selbstvernichtungsfrage ist kein Schlussbeispiel, sondern die globale Belastungsprobe dafür, ob kulturelle Bindung mit der Reichweite destruktiver Handlungsmacht Schritt halten kann.
Religiöses Gefühl und behauptete Weltzweckmäßigkeit werden als unmittelbare Erkenntnisquellen ausgeschlossen. ; Trace Type — Negative
Ausgeschlossen ist ein von Bedürftigkeit, Trieb, Objektbindung und Autorität unabhängiges oder sich selbst vollständig transparentes Subjekt. ; Trace Type — Negative
Ausgeschlossen sind dauerhaftes Glück, teleologischer Kulturfortschritt und jede fortschreitende Aufhebung des Grundkonflikts. ; Trace Type — Negative
Ausgeschlossen ist eine Kultur, die Schutz, Freiheit und Gemeinschaft ohne Triebopfer, Aggressionsverlagerung oder Schuld erzeugt. ; Trace Type — Negative
Rationales Eigeninteresse und moralische Liebesgebote werden als hinreichende Grundlagen dauerhafter Großgemeinschaften verworfen. ; Trace Type — Negative
Eigentum, Erziehung oder einzelne Institutionen dürfen Aggression weder ursprünglich erzeugen noch restlos erklären. ; Trace Type — Negative

Normative Geltung beweist weder psychische Vollziehbarkeit noch therapeutische Wirksamkeit, und die Individualdiagnostik lässt sich nicht maßstabsneutral in eine kollektive Therapie überführen. ; Trace Type — Negative
Damit die Gesamtarchitektur trägt, muss kostenloser Schutz unmöglich sein; jede Abwehr muss neue Bindungen, Versagungen oder Rückkehrwirkungen erzeugen können. ; Trace Type — Negative

Libido und Destruktion dürfen weder unbegrenzt verfügbar noch durch kulturelle Hemmung vernichtbar sein, weil sonst Umverteilung und Rückwendung ihre generative Funktion verlieren. ; Trace Type — Negative
Kultur darf nicht außerhalb des Triebkonflikts stehen; eine neutrale Befriedungsinstanz würde die Rekursion von Bindung, Verzicht und Aggressionsverlagerung aufheben. ; Trace Type — Negative

Natürliche Moral und ein transparentes Inneres müssen ausgeschlossen bleiben, weil Schuld und Autorität sonst nicht als unbewusste, verinnerlichte Trieboperationen rekonstruierbar wären. ; Trace Type — Negative

Kulturelle Erweiterung darf exklusive Bindungen nicht unverändert bewahren, und psychische Mechanismen dürfen beim Maßstabswechsel nicht ohne Zielverschiebung identisch bleiben. ; Trace Type — Negative
Ein externer Normalitätsmaßstab und eine therapiefähige kollektive Autorität müssen fehlen; andernfalls würde die Diagnose in eine souveräne Gesamtsteuerung umschlagen. ; Trace Type — Negative
Die tiefste versperrte Möglichkeit ist die terminale Versöhnung von Lust, Realität, Freiheit, Eros und Destruktion. ; Trace Type — Negative
Nicht verfügbar ist eine Großgemeinschaft, die exklusive Liebe bewahrt, Aggression bindet und dennoch weder Ausschluss noch Schuld produziert. ; Trace Type — Negative
Nicht verfügbar ist ein vollständig souveränes, tugendhaft entlastetes und innerlich transparentes Subjekt. ; Trace Type — Negative

Nicht verfügbar sind eine positive isolierte Erkenntnis des Todestriebs und eine unbetroffene Normalität, von der aus seine kulturellen Wirkungen abschließend bewertet werden könnten. ; Trace Type — Negative
Nicht verfügbar ist eine Geschichtsteleologie, die Opfer kompensiert, den Kulturverlauf rechtfertigt und den Sieg des Eros garantiert. ; Trace Type — Negative

Die Kostenförmigkeit individueller Abwehr und die Endlichkeit kulturell verfügbarer Libido machen jeden Schutzgewinn zu einer Neuverteilung von Befriedigung, Bindung und destruktivem Risiko. ; Trace Type — Composite
Psychische Grenze, Recht und Über-Ich bilden eine verteilte Grenzmaschine, die äußere Macht in soziale Selbstbeschränkung und schließlich in innere Überwachung transformiert. ; Trace Type — Composite

Religiöse Schutzordnung und moralische Gewissensordnung sind homologe Autoritätsformationen: Beide transformieren Abhängigkeit in bindende Deutung, verlieren aber dadurch ihren Anspruch auf transzendente oder natürliche Selbstbegründung. ; Trace Type — Composite

Kultur beantwortet soziale Aggressionsgefahr, indem sie äußere Destruktion in Schuld und Selbstbestrafung umleitet; ihr Schutzapparat produziert dadurch das Unbehagen, das er regulieren soll. ; Trace Type — Composite

Die Erweiterung kultureller Einheit verlangt zugleich libidinöse Umverteilung und verschärfte innere Einschränkung, sodass Eros nicht nur verbindet, sondern mittelbar die Schuldökonomie vergrößert. ; Trace Type — Composite

Die Ortswechsel der Aggression bilden einen Eskalationspfad von zwischenmenschlicher Gefahr über Selbstbestrafung zur technisch potenzierten Vernichtungsfähigkeit der Gattung. ; Trace Type — Composite

Politische Reform kann Rechtsformen, Verteilungen und Aggressionsinstrumente verändern, aber keine vollständige Emanzipation vom Triebkonflikt garantieren; Handlungsmacht bleibt kanalbezogen statt souverän. ; Trace Type — Tension

Die Verbindung von genetischer Kritik, indirekter Todestrieb-Rekonstruktion und fehlendem kulturäußerem Maßstab erzeugt eine reflexive Erkenntnismethode, die starke Diagnosen erlaubt, aber ihre eigenen Voraussetzungen nicht neutralisieren kann. ; Trace Type — Tension

Universale Liebes- und Moralgebote können ihre Gegenkräfte verstärken, weil äußere Solidarität Aggression verlagert und psychisch undurchführbare Forderungen Schuld, Auflehnung oder Ausschluss erzeugen. ; Trace Type — Tension
Die Entkopplung technischer Macht von Glück und Triebbeherrschung transformiert das Kulturproblem von einer Verzichtsbilanz in eine Überlebensfrage. ; Trace Type — Composite
Realität erscheint als geschichtete Umwandlungsmaschine, die Druck in Grenze, Bindung, Recht, Verzicht, Schuld und technische Macht überführt und dabei neue Druckformen erzeugt.
Das Subjekt wird zu einem endlichen Relais, an dem Libido zwischen Ich und Objekten, Aggression zwischen Außenwelt und Selbst sowie Autorität zwischen sozialer Sanktion und innerem Gebot zirkuliert.
Kausalität wird geschichtet und zirkulär: Triebe liefern energetische Bedingungen, Institutionen bestimmen Richtungen, und die Resultate institutioneller Hemmung wirken auf die Triebökonomie zurück.
Zeit wird zur Persistenz unter Mutation und zur Akkumulation ungelöster Konflikte; spätere Ordnungen ersetzen frühere Strukturen nicht, sondern reaktivieren sie auf erhöhtem Gefahrenniveau.
Politik wird als begrenzte, aber reale Veränderung von Bindungen, Machtverteilungen und Aggressionskanälen rekonstruierbar, ohne den Status einer vollständigen Triebtherapie zu erhalten.

Ethik wird zur Diagnose ihrer psychischen Vollzugsbedingungen und tatsächlichen Aggressionseffekte; ein Gebot ist nicht allein nach seinem normativen Inhalt, sondern nach seinen Schuld- und Widerstandsproduktionen zu beurteilen.

Handlungsmacht besteht in partieller Navigation, Umlenkung und institutioneller Korrektur; sie bleibt wirksam, besitzt aber weder einen triebfreien Außenpunkt noch eine Erfolgsgarantie gegen Selbstvernichtung.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Unlust erzeugt Grenze und Schutz; Schutz erzeugt Abhängigkeit und Versagung; diese Kosten erzeugen neue Unlust und legitimieren weitere Schutzleistungen.
Das unerfüllbare Glücksprogramm erzeugt pluralisierte Lebenstechniken, deren Scheitern Kultur und Kompensation aufruft, ohne eine allgemeine Glückstechnik hervorzubringen.
Kulturelle Expansion beschränkt exklusive Libido, schwächt damit eine Quelle ihrer eigenen Bindungskraft und steigert den Bedarf an zielgehemmten Ersatzbindungen und zusätzlichen Normen.
Aggression erzeugt Hemmung; Hemmung erzeugt Innenwendung; Innenwendung verstärkt das Über-Ich; dessen Forderungen erzeugen weiteren Verzicht und zusätzliche Aggressionsübertragung.
Innere Gruppenbindung externalisiert Aggression, Außenfeindschaft verdichtet die Gruppe, und die verdichtete Gruppe reproduziert die Grenze, aus der ihre Kohäsion hervorgeht.

Überfordernde Ethik bildet einen Selbstverstärkungskreis: Verschärfte Gebote erzeugen Nichtbefolgbarkeit, Schuld oder Auflehnung, die als moralisches Defizit gelesen und mit neuen Geboten beantwortet werden.
Technische Naturbeherrschung steigert die Reichweite fortbestehender Aggression schneller, als kulturelle Selbstbindung gesichert werden kann, und eskaliert den Triebkonflikt zur Gattungsgefahr.
Der übergeordnete Attraktor verbindet Kompensation mit dem Eros-Todestrieb-Gegensatz: Kultur sucht Ersatz für verlangten Verzicht, während jede Bindung Destruktion lediglich reorganisiert.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Behauptete Wahrheit → genetische und funktionale Rekonstruktion → Entzug religiöser, teleologischer oder moralischer Selbstbeglaubigung.
Unerfüllbares Glücksprogramm → pluralisierte Abwehrtechniken → spezifische Kosten → Übergang von individueller Lebensführung zur Kulturökonomie.
Hilflosigkeit und Leidensdruck → kollektiver Schutzapparat → Recht und Triebeinschränkung → Kultur als notwendige und endogene Leidensproduktion.
Endliche Libido + kultureller Skalierungsbedarf → Beschneidung exklusiver Bindung → zielgehemmte Umverteilung → Eros als Prinzip extensiver Einheitsbildung.
Primäre Feindseligkeit → unvollständige institutionelle Hemmung → metapsychologischer Rest → Todestrieb als verborgener Grund der Destruktion.
Äußere Aggressionshemmung → Innenwendung → Über-Ich → Triebverzicht als Ursache weiterer Gewissensstrenge → rekursive Schuldsteigerung.
Individuelle Autoritätsverinnerlichung → kontrollierte Skalierung zum Kultur-Über-Ich → Ethik als bindende, aber potenziell pathogene Aggressionsabwehr.
Technische Naturbeherrschung + unaufgehobene Destruktion → globale Selbstvernichtungsfähigkeit → Eros als notwendige, aber nicht sieggarantierte Gegenkraft.
Religiöser Wahrheitsanspruch → Psychogenese der Schutzsehnsucht → unerfüllbares Glücksprogramm → kostenförmige Lebenstechniken → Kultur als Schutz und Versagung → Kultur als Triebmetabolismus.
Endliche Libido → kulturelle Einheitsbildung → primäre Aggression → Todestrieb → Innenwendung → Über-Ich und Schuld → technische Selbstvernichtungsfähigkeit.
Kultur benötigt Bindung → beschädigt deren unmittelbare Formen → reproduziert ihr eigenes Zwangsmittel → endet in einer offenen Gegenanstrengung des Eros.
Religion und Moral werden von privilegierten Wahrheits- oder Wertordnungen zu genealogisch rekonstruierbaren Techniken von Schutz, Abhängigkeit und Autoritätsbindung umkartiert.
Der Gegensatz von Natur und Kultur kollabiert: Kultur erscheint als historische Organisation natürlicher Triebkräfte und nicht als deren äußere Überwindung.
Individuum und Gesellschaft werden als verschiedene Maßstäbe derselben Regulationsarchitektur lesbar, ohne ihre Zielordnungen oder Prozessformen vollständig gleichzusetzen.
Liebe und Aggression verlieren den Status reiner Gegensätze, weil Bindung destruktive Legierungen enthalten und Eros über Einschränkung, Schuld und Außenfeindschaft vermittelt sein kann.
Recht, Reform und Ethik werden von Erlösungsinstanzen zu Kanaltechniken umklassifiziert, deren Wert an psychischer Vollziehbarkeit und tatsächlichen Aggressionseffekten hängt.
Glück und Fortschritt werden entkoppelt: episodische Befriedigung eignet sich nicht als Kulturmaß, während technischer Fortschritt selbst zum Aggressionsmultiplikator werden kann.
Schuld wird von objektiver Tatbewertung in eine psychische Topik umkartiert, und Gewissen erscheint als institutionalisierte Aggression gegen das Ich.
Die angemessene Lektüre wird residual, rekursiv und maßstabssensibel, weil tragende Kräfte indirekt erscheinen und begriffliche Wiederkehr häufig einen Funktions- oder Phasenwechsel bezeichnet.
Auf der Surface level verbinden sich religiöse Erfahrung, Glückstechniken, Familie, Sexualität, Moral, Schuld und technische Vernichtungsmacht zu Erscheinungsformen eines gemeinsamen Kulturproblems.
Auf der Structural level operieren Arbeit, Recht, Libidoumleitung, Aggressionshemmung, Über-Ich und Schuld als gekoppelte Mechanismen räumlicher Verschiebung und zeitlicher Akkumulation.
Auf der Metastrategic level werden Wahrheitsanspruch, Moralgebot und Reformmodell durch genetische Prüfung, Kostenvergleich, Energieverwaltung und Analyse psychischer Durchführbarkeit ersetzt.
Auf der Ontological / Temporal level ist Realität nicht auf Glück eingerichtet; Leben und Geschichte bestehen als nichtteleologisch entschiedene Auseinandersetzung von Bindung und Auflösung.
Auf der Methodological / Performative level vollzieht die Argumentform ihre These durch Entprivilegierung, genealogischen Abstieg, wiederholte Rückkehr, Kausalumkehr und Maßstabsskalierung.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Der Todestrieb ist für die terminale Architektur unverzichtbar, bleibt aber nur indirekt in Mischphänomenen zugänglich; dieselben Phänomene begründen und bestätigen daher den angenommenen Trieb. ; Trace Type — Tension
Die Unterscheidung zwischen reformierbarem Kulturleid und strukturell notwendigem Triebverzicht bleibt politisch unverzichtbar, besitzt jedoch kein stabiles Kriterium. ; Trace Type — Tension

Die Analogie von Individual- und Kulturentwicklung ermöglicht das Kultur-Über-Ich, wird aber durch Zielasymmetrie, ungesicherte Skalierung und fehlende Prozessidentität begrenzt. ; Trace Type — Tension

Die Architektur kritisiert ungerechte Einschränkung und pathogene Ethik, obwohl sie einen kulturäußeren Normalitätsmaßstab verwirft; ihre normative Brücke bleibt deshalb operativ, aber unbegründet. ; Trace Type — Tension

Liebe und Aggression besitzen richtungs- und maßstabsabhängige Valenzen: Liebe kann binden und Schuld vermitteln, Aggression kann auflösen, Selbsterhaltung fördern oder Gruppen integrieren. ; Trace Type — Tension
Die offene Gegenanstrengung des Eros begründet begrenzte Handlungsmacht, erlaubt aber keine Deduktion des technologischen Ausgangs oder des endgültigen Kräfteverhältnisses. ; Trace Type — Tension
Religiöse Erfahrung mutiert vom möglichen Transzendenzzeugnis zum psychischen Rest früher Grenzlosigkeit und danach zum Modell institutionalisierter Schutzabhängigkeit. ; Trace Type — Tension
Grenzbildung mutiert von der Ich-Außen-Unterscheidung zur rechtlichen Selbstbeschränkung und schließlich zur innerpsychischen Teilung zwischen Ich und Über-Ich. ; Trace Type — Tension
Liebe mutiert von konkreter familialer Bindung über kulturell umgeleitete Libido zum ontologisch erweiterten Erosprinzip. ; Trace Type — Tension
Aggression mutiert von sozialer Feindseligkeit über externalisierte Todestriebtätigkeit zur inneren Strafgewalt und technisch potenzierten Gattungsgefahr. ; Trace Type — Tension
Triebverzicht mutiert von einer Wirkung äußerer Autoritätsangst zur Ursache zusätzlicher Über-Ich-Strenge und schließt damit die Schuldrekursion. ; Trace Type — Tension
Fortschritt mutiert von Macht- und Integrationsgewinn zu einer offenen Risikostruktur, sobald technische Naturbeherrschung globale Selbstvernichtungsfähigkeit erzeugt. ; Trace Type — Tension

Realität erscheint als verschachtelte Grenz-, Strom- und Umleitungsmaschine, in der Eros Einheiten bindet, Destruktion sie löst und Kultur beide Kräfte durch Institutionen und innere Instanzen kanalisiert.
Das Subjekt ist kein verfügungsfähiges Zentrum, sondern ein umkämpfter Umschlagplatz von Körper, Objektlibido, Destruktion, äußerer Autorität und Über-Ich.
Zeit ist asymmetrische rekursive Akkumulation: Lust bleibt episodisch, frühere Autorität wirkt im Über-Ich fort, und derselbe Antagonismus kehrt mit wachsender technischer Reichweite wieder.
Möglich bleibt keine Flucht aus der Triebordnung, sondern nur revidierbare Navigation zwischen Bindung, Verteilung, institutioneller Korrektur und nicht garantiert beherrschbarer Destruktion.

Die extrahierten Axiome reichen aus, um die Bewegung von religiöser Schutzsehnsucht über Glücksökonomie und kulturelle Triebverwaltung bis zu Schuldrekursion und technischer Selbstvernichtungsgefahr zu rekonstruieren.

Unterbestimmt bleiben das tatsächliche Vorkommen einzelner Ursprungserfahrungen, die unabhängige Identifikation des Todestriebs, die Gewichtung der Über-Ich-Quellen und der Übergang zur kollektiven Diagnose.

Das System ist nur konditional kohärent: Es verlangt die Trennung von Erlebnis, Genese und Funktion sowie die Annahme indirekt erschließbarer Triebkräfte und einer kontrollierten, nicht identischen Skalierung.
Die Architektur ist am stärksten in der skalierbaren Verbindung von Grenzbildung, kostenförmiger Abwehr, endlicher Libido, Aggressionshemmung, Innenwendung und rekursiver Gewissensverschärfung.

Die Rekonstruktion bewahrt die tatsächliche Bewegung nur, wenn genealogische Hypothesen als Trägerschichten, wiederholte Begriffe als Mutationen und der Triebverzicht als kausal umkehrender Mechanismus behandelt werden.

Einer vollständigen axiomatischen Reduktion widerstehen nichtutilitäre Kulturwerte, der normative Überschuss der Gerechtigkeit, die indirekte Evidenz des Todestriebs und der unentscheidbare Ausgang des Eros-Destruktions-Konflikts.

translations.title: Das Unbehagen in der Kultur (1930) · OCR review

items.text: The system examines why culture is at once indispensable protection against helplessness, the force of nature, and human aggression, as well as an independent source of frustration, guilt, and unhappiness.

The global thesis is that psychic and cultural orders do not eliminate drives, but redistribute them through boundary formation, binding, restriction, displacement, and internalization in such a way that every stabilization generates new costs.

The argument becomes a genetic, functional, and metapsychological reconstruction that separates religious certainty, the claim to happiness, the cultural ideal, and moral guilt from their self-authentication and traces them back to their psychic operations.

The movement leads from psychic helplessness and the longing for protection, through the unfulfillable happiness programme, to culture as a drive economy, from there to primary aggression, and finally to the inner punitive force of the superego.

This movement is recursive and escalating because protection produces dependency, binding renunciation, the inhibition of aggression inward turning, and obedience to conscience additional severity of conscience.

Individual psyche, social institution, and cultural history do not constitute separate domains, but different scales of a single architecture of redirection, whose scaling preserves functions while shifting aims.

Technical progress does not close this architecture but intensifies it, because increasing power of disposal neither guarantees happiness nor is linked to a proportional increase in the cultural binding of aggression.

The conclusion remains open and diagnostic: a final reconciliation of pleasure, freedom, security, cultural unity, Eros, and destruction is excluded, while the outcome of their conflict remains undecidable.
[Persistent] Subjective intensity, collective assent, moral validity, and asserted purposiveness do not legitimize any content without genetic, functional, and economic reconstruction.
[Persistent] The subject is not a sovereign origin, but a stratified point of conversion of bodily needs, libidinal cathexes, destructive directions, external authority, and internalized demands.
[Persistent] Culture secures larger communities through protection, law, binding, and drive restriction, yet produces its own forms of suffering precisely through these means of integration.
[Emergent] Every psychic or cultural protective achievement is a redistribution of limited satisfaction, binding, and aggression; it can diminish dangers without abolishing dependency or drive costs.

[Terminal] The happiness programme posited by the pleasure principle is neither durably nor universally fulfillable, and cultural progress cannot transform its unfulfillability into a secured reconciliation.

[Mutating] Love mutates from exclusive object- and family-binding, through aim-inhibited social binding, into the Eros principle of cultural unification, whereby every expansion must curtail its intensive initial forms.

[Mutating] Aggression escalates from interpersonal hostility to a manifestation of the death drive, is culturally redirected outward or inward, and is potentiated by technical power up to possible self-destruction.
[Mutating] Boundary formation mutates from the psychic distinction between self and outside, through law and drive restriction, into the internalized authority of the superego.

[Attractor] After the internalization of authority, drive renunciation becomes a recursive intensifier of guilt, because every new renunciation transfers further aggression to the agency that demands it.
[Attractor] Cultural history is the interminable working-out of the conflict between unifying Eros and binding-dissolving destruction on psychic, institutional, and human-historical scales.
[Emergent] Cultural time is non-teleological and recursive: earlier formations remain effective under functional mutation, while unresolved aggression, guilt, and technical reach accumulate.
[Terminal] Technical mastery of nature increases agency without proportional psychic self-binding; therefore, the architecture ends in an open conflict of survival, not in a guarantee of progress.

Religion does not recur as an autonomous final object, but after its psychogenetic reinterpretation is absorbed into the more general architecture of helplessness, dependency on protection, and attachment to authority.
The ego boundary migrates from individual genesis into law and social restriction and finally returns as a psychic inner boundary between ego and superego.
Happiness shifts from an alleged purpose of life to episodic satisfaction and then to a negative balance-sheet item of cultural integration and increasing technical risk.

Love retains its binding function, but expands its scope from exclusive proximity, through redistributed libido, to the supra-individual Eros that produces cultural unity and thereby demands additional restriction.

Aggression preserves its energetic identity, but mutates ontologically and topically from external hostility, through the death drive and inner punitive force, to technologically intensified power of self-destruction.

Restriction escalates from adaptation to reality and legal binding, through sexual and aggressive inhibition, to causal reversal, in which enacted renunciation strengthens the agency of conscience that demands it.

Authority changes its place from external protective and punitive power to the individual superego and the cultural superego; morality thereby loses its natural valence and becomes a technique of drive administration.

Progress recurs with reversed valence: what initially increases power of disposal and protection ultimately becomes a multiplier of the aggression whose cultural binding does not grow correspondingly.

The actual occurrence and precise genesis of the oceanic feeling remain local; at the whole-book level, only the methodological separation of experiential intensity, origin, function, and truth-validity scales.

Individual techniques of happiness and cultural traits remain local typologies; globally, only the rule carries that every technique produces a particular distribution of relief, dependency, and costs.

Organic speculations about origins and the primal-father murder remain genealogical frameworks of the lower level; what scales upward is the connection of ambivalence, identification, aggression, and institutionalized restriction.

Monogamy, heterosexuality, and the order of property remain concrete normative or test cases; globally relevant is the difference between historically variable channels of aggression and a drive constitution irreducible to institutions.
Sadism, masochism, and clinical symptom divisions remain local means of justification; at the whole-book level, the indirect apprehension of mixed drive forces and inhibited aggression scales.
The question of technological self-destruction is not a concluding example, but the global stress test of whether cultural binding can keep pace with the reach of destructive agency.
Religious feeling and asserted purposiveness of the world are excluded as immediate sources of knowledge. ; Trace Type — Negative
Excluded is a subject independent of neediness, drive, object-binding, and authority, or one wholly transparent to itself. ; Trace Type — Negative
Excluded are lasting happiness, teleological cultural progress, and every progressive overcoming of the fundamental conflict. ; Trace Type — Negative
Excluded is a culture that produces protection, freedom, and community without drive sacrifice, displacement of aggression, or guilt. ; Trace Type — Negative
Rational self-interest and moral commandments of love are rejected as sufficient foundations of lasting large communities. ; Trace Type — Negative
Property, education, or individual institutions may neither originally produce aggression nor exhaustively explain it. ; Trace Type — Negative

Normative validity proves neither psychic feasibility nor therapeutic efficacy, and individual diagnosis cannot be transferred into collective therapy in a scale-neutral manner. ; Trace Type — Negative
For the overall architecture to hold, cost-free protection must be impossible; every defense must be capable of producing new bindings, frustrations, or return effects. ; Trace Type — Negative

Libido and destruction may be neither infinitely available nor destructible through cultural inhibition, for otherwise redistribution and turning-back lose their generative function. ; Trace Type — Negative
Culture may not stand outside the drive conflict; a neutral agency of pacification would abolish the recursion of binding, renunciation, and displacement of aggression. ; Trace Type — Negative

Natural morality and a transparent inner life must remain excluded, because otherwise guilt and authority could not be reconstructed as unconscious, internalized drive operations. ; Trace Type — Negative
Cultural expansion may not preserve exclusive bindings unchanged, and psychic mechanisms may not remain identical during a change of scale without a shift of aim. ; Trace Type — Negative
An external standard of normality and a therapeutically capable collective authority must be absent; otherwise diagnosis would turn into sovereign overall control. ; Trace Type — Negative
The deepest barred possibility is the terminal reconciliation of pleasure, reality, freedom, Eros, and destruction. ; Trace Type — Negative
Unavailable is a large community that preserves exclusive love, binds aggression, and nevertheless produces neither exclusion nor guilt. ; Trace Type — Negative
Unavailable is a wholly sovereign subject, virtuously relieved and inwardly transparent. ; Trace Type — Negative
Unavailable are a positive isolated cognition of the death drive and an unaffected normality from which its cultural effects could be conclusively assessed. ; Trace Type — Negative
Unavailable is a teleology of history that compensates sacrifices, justifies the course of culture, and guarantees the victory of Eros. ; Trace Type — Negative

The cost-character of individual defense and the finitude of culturally available libido make every gain in protection a redistribution of satisfaction, binding, and destructive risk. ; Trace Type — Composite
Psychic boundary, law, and superego form a distributed boundary machine that transforms external power into social self-restriction and finally into inner surveillance. ; Trace Type — Composite

Religious protective order and moral order of conscience are homologous formations of authority: both transform dependency into binding interpretation, but thereby lose their claim to transcendent or natural self-foundation. ; Trace Type — Composite

Culture responds to the danger of social aggression by redirecting external destruction into guilt and self-punishment; its protective apparatus thereby produces the discontent it is meant to regulate. ; Trace Type — Composite

The expansion of cultural unity simultaneously requires libidinal redistribution and intensified inner restriction, such that Eros not only binds but indirectly enlarges the economy of guilt. ; Trace Type — Composite

The changes of place of aggression form a path of escalation from interpersonal danger, through self-punishment, to the technologically potentiated destructive capacity of the species. ; Trace Type — Composite

Political reform can alter legal forms, distributions, and instruments of aggression, but cannot guarantee complete emancipation from drive conflict; agency remains channel-specific rather than sovereign. ; Trace Type — Tension

The connection of genetic critique, indirect reconstruction of the death drive, and the absence of a standard external to culture produces a reflexive method of knowledge that permits strong diagnoses but cannot neutralize its own presuppositions. ; Trace Type — Tension

Universal commandments of love and morality can reinforce their counterforces, because external solidarity displaces aggression and psychically unfulfillable demands produce guilt, rebellion, or exclusion. ; Trace Type — Tension
The decoupling of technical power from happiness and drive mastery transforms the problem of culture from a balance of renunciation into a question of survival. ; Trace Type — Composite
Reality appears as a stratified machine of transformation that converts pressure into boundary, binding, law, renunciation, guilt, and technical power, while producing new forms of pressure.
The subject becomes a finite relay through which libido circulates between ego and objects, aggression between outer world and self, and authority between social sanction and inner command.
Causality becomes stratified and circular: drives provide energetic conditions, institutions determine directions, and the results of institutional inhibition act back upon the drive economy.
Time becomes persistence under mutation and the accumulation of unresolved conflicts; later orders do not replace earlier structures, but reactivate them at an elevated level of danger.
Politics becomes reconstructible as limited but real alteration of bindings, distributions of power, and channels of aggression, without receiving the status of a complete therapy of drives.

Ethics becomes diagnosis of its conditions of psychic enactment and actual effects of aggression; a commandment is to be judged not solely by its normative content, but by its productions of guilt and resistance.

Agency consists in partial navigation, redirection, and institutional correction; it remains effective, but possesses neither a drive-free external standpoint nor a guarantee of success against self-destruction.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Unpleasure produces boundary and protection; protection produces dependency and frustration; these costs produce new unpleasure and legitimize further protective measures.
The unfulfillable happiness programme produces pluralized techniques of life whose failure calls forth culture and compensation without producing a general technique of happiness.
Cultural expansion restricts exclusive libido, thereby weakens a source of its own binding force, and increases the need for aim-inhibited substitute bindings and additional norms.
Aggression produces inhibition; inhibition produces inward turning; inward turning strengthens the superego; its demands produce further renunciation and additional transfer of aggression.
Inner group binding externalizes aggression, hostility toward outsiders condenses the group, and the condensed group reproduces the boundary from which its cohesion arises.
Overburdening ethics forms a self-reinforcing circle: intensified commandments produce noncompliance, guilt, or rebellion, which are read as moral deficiency and answered with new commandments.
Technical mastery of nature increases the reach of persisting aggression faster than cultural self-binding can be secured, and escalates drive conflict into a danger to the species.
The higher-order attractor connects compensation with the Eros–death-drive opposition: culture seeks substitutes for demanded renunciation, while every binding merely reorganizes destruction.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Asserted truth → genetic and functional reconstruction → withdrawal of religious, teleological, or moral self-authentication.
Unfulfillable happiness programme → pluralized techniques of defense → specific costs → transition from individual conduct of life to cultural economy.
Helplessness and pressure of suffering → collective protective apparatus → law and drive restriction → culture as necessary and endogenous production of suffering.
Finite libido + need for cultural scaling → curtailment of exclusive binding → aim-inhibited redistribution → Eros as principle of extensive unification.
Primary hostility → incomplete institutional inhibition → metapsychological remainder → death drive as the hidden ground of destruction.
External inhibition of aggression → inward turning → superego → drive renunciation as cause of further severity of conscience → recursive intensification of guilt.
Individual internalization of authority → controlled scaling to the cultural superego → ethics as binding, yet potentially pathogenic, defense against aggression.
Technical mastery of nature + unabolished destruction → global capacity for self-destruction → Eros as a necessary counterforce, but one not guaranteed victory.

Religious claim to truth → psychogenesis of the longing for protection → unfulfillable happiness programme → cost-form techniques of life → culture as protection and frustration → culture as drive metabolism.
Finite libido → cultural unification → primary aggression → death drive → inward turning → superego and guilt → technical capacity for self-destruction.
Culture requires binding → damages its immediate forms → reproduces its own means of coercion → ends in an open counter-effort of Eros.
Religion and morality are remapped from privileged orders of truth or value into genealogically reconstructible techniques of protection, dependency, and attachment to authority.
The opposition between nature and culture collapses: culture appears as the historical organization of natural drive forces and not as their external overcoming.
Individual and society become legible as different scales of the same regulatory architecture, without completely equating their orders of aim or forms of process.
Love and aggression lose the status of pure opposites, because binding can contain destructive alloys and Eros can be mediated through restriction, guilt, and hostility toward outsiders.
Law, reform, and ethics are reclassified from agencies of redemption into channel techniques, whose value depends on psychic feasibility and actual effects of aggression.
Happiness and progress are decoupled: episodic satisfaction is unsuitable as a measure of culture, while technical progress itself can become a multiplier of aggression.
Guilt is remapped from objective assessment of an act into a psychic topic, and conscience appears as institutionalized aggression against the ego.
The appropriate reading becomes residual, recursive, and scale-sensitive, because supporting forces appear indirectly and conceptual recurrence often denotes a change of function or phase.
At the Surface level, religious experience, techniques of happiness, family, sexuality, morality, guilt, and technical destructive power combine into manifestations of a common problem of culture.
At the Structural level, labor, law, libidinal redirection, inhibition of aggression, superego, and guilt operate as coupled mechanisms of spatial displacement and temporal accumulation.

At the Metastrategic level, claims to truth, moral commandments, and models of reform are replaced by genetic examination, comparison of costs, energy administration, and analysis of psychic feasibility.
At the Ontological / Temporal level, reality is not arranged for happiness; life and history consist as a non-teleologically decided confrontation between binding and dissolution.
At the Methodological / Performative level, the argumentative form enacts its thesis through deprivileging, genealogical descent, repeated return, causal reversal, and scaling of measure.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The death drive is indispensable to the terminal architecture, but remains accessible only indirectly in mixed phenomena; the same phenomena therefore ground and confirm the assumed drive. ; Trace Type — Tension
The distinction between reformable cultural suffering and structurally necessary drive renunciation remains politically indispensable, but possesses no stable criterion. ; Trace Type — Tension
The analogy between individual and cultural development enables the cultural superego, but is limited by asymmetry of aims, unsecured scaling, and lack of process identity. ; Trace Type — Tension

The architecture criticizes unjust restriction and pathogenic ethics although it rejects a standard of normality external to culture; its normative bridge therefore remains operative, but ungrounded. ; Trace Type — Tension
Love and aggression possess direction- and scale-dependent valences: love can bind and mediate guilt, aggression can dissolve, promote self-preservation, or integrate groups. ; Trace Type — Tension
The open counter-effort of Eros grounds limited agency, but permits no deduction of the technological outcome or of the final relation of forces. ; Trace Type — Tension

Religious experience mutates from possible testimony of transcendence into the psychic remnant of earlier boundlessness and then into the model of institutionalized dependency on protection. ; Trace Type — Tension
Boundary formation mutates from the ego–outside distinction to legal self-restriction and finally to intrapsychic division between ego and superego. ; Trace Type — Tension
Love mutates from concrete familial binding, through culturally redirected libido, into the ontologically expanded Eros principle. ; Trace Type — Tension
Aggression mutates from social hostility, through externalized death-drive activity, into inner punitive force and technologically potentiated danger to the species. ; Trace Type — Tension
Drive renunciation mutates from an effect of fear of external authority into the cause of additional superego severity and thereby closes the recursion of guilt. ; Trace Type — Tension
Progress mutates from a gain in power and integration into an open risk structure once technical mastery of nature produces global capacity for self-destruction. ; Trace Type — Tension

Reality appears as a nested machine of boundaries, flows, and redirections, in which Eros binds unities, destruction dissolves them, and culture channels both forces through institutions and inner agencies.
The subject is not a center capable of disposal, but a contested switching point of body, object-libido, destruction, external authority, and superego.
Time is asymmetric recursive accumulation: pleasure remains episodic, earlier authority persists in the superego, and the same antagonism recurs with increasing technical reach.
What remains possible is not escape from the order of drives, but only revisable navigation between binding, distribution, institutional correction, and destruction not guaranteed to be controllable.

The extracted axioms suffice to reconstruct the movement from religious longing for protection, through the economy of happiness and cultural drive administration, to the recursion of guilt and the danger of technical self-destruction.

What remains underdetermined are the actual occurrence of individual experiences of origin, the independent identification of the death drive, the weighting of the sources of the superego, and the transition to collective diagnosis.

The system is only conditionally coherent: it requires the separation of experience, genesis, and function, as well as the assumption of indirectly apprehensible drive forces and controlled, non-identical scaling.

The architecture is strongest in the scalable connection of boundary formation, cost-form defense, finite libido, inhibition of aggression, inward turning, and recursive intensification of conscience.

The reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if genealogical hypotheses are treated as supporting layers, repeated concepts as mutations, and drive renunciation as a causally reversing mechanism.

Resisting complete axiomatic reduction are non-utilitarian cultural values, the normative surplus of justice, the indirect evidence of the death drive, and the undecidable outcome of the Eros–destruction conflict.

<!-- CARE_TEI_PAGE {"facs": "tcp:49588:44"} --> <!-- CARE_TEI_PAGE {"n": "1", "facs": "tcp:49588:44"} --> 

## A TRUE RELATION OF Dr. DEES Actions, with spirits. 

 

[SOURCE DIVISION: book]

 

## Liber Mysteriorum (& Sancti) parallelus Novalisque.  [Note:  D. Is Dr. Dee, E. K. Edward Kellet See the Preface.]  Lesden MAY 28. 1583.

 

Δ. AS J. and E. K. sate discoursing of the Noble Polonian Albertus  [Note: A. L.]  Lasci his great honour here with us obteined, his great good liking of all States of the people, of them that either see him or hear of him, and again how much I was beholding to God that his heart should so fervently favour me, and that he doth so much strive to suppresse and confound the malice and envie of my Country-men against me, for my better credit winning or recovering to do God better service hereafter thereby, &c. Suddenly, there seemed to come out of my Oratory a Spirituall creature, like a pretty girle of 7 or 9 yeares of age, attired on her head with her hair rowled up before, and hanging down very long behind, with a gown of  [Note: Green and red.]  Sey, .....changeable green and red, and with a train she seemed to play up and down..... like, and seemed to go in and out behind my books, lying on heaps, the biggest .....and as she should ever go between them, the books seemed to give place sufficiently, dis.... one heap from the other, while she passed between  • hem: And so I considered, and ..... the diverse reports which E. K. made unto me of this pretty maiden, and .....

 

Δ. I said ..... Whose maiden are you?

 

Δ. Sh. ..... VVhose man are you? 

 

Δ. I am the servant of God both by my bound duty, and also (I hope) by his Adoption.

 

A voyce. ..... You shall be beaten if you tell. 

 

..... Am not I a fine Maiden? Give me leave to play in your house, my Mother told me she would come and dwell here.

 

Δ. She went up and down with most lively gestures of a young girle, playing by her selfe, and diverse times another spake to her from the corner of my study by a great Perspective­glasse, but none was seen beside her selfe.

 

..... Shall I? I will (Now she seemed to answer one in the foresaid Corner of the Study)

 

..... I pray you let me tarry a little [speaking to one in the foresaid Corner]

 

Δ. Tell me who you are?

 

..... I pray you let me play with you a little, and I will tell you who I am.

 

Δ. In the name of Jesus then tell me.  [Note: Jesus.]  

 

..... I rejoyce in the name of Jesus, and I am a poor little Maiden, Madini, I am the last but one of my Mothers children, I have little Baby-children at home.  [Note: Proles ipsius Madini. ]  

 

Δ. Where is your home?

 

 Ma..... I dare not tell you where I dwell, I shall be beaten.

 

Δ. You shall not be beaten for telling the truth to them that love the truth, to the eter­nal truth all Creatures must be obedient.

 

 Ma. ..... I warrant you I will be obedient. My Sisters say they must all come and dwell with you.  [Note:  Madini her six Sisters.]  

 <!-- CARE_TEI_PAGE {"n": "2", "facs": "tcp:49588:45"} --> 

Δ. I desire that they who love God should dwell with me, and I with them.

 

 Ma. ..... I love you now you talke of God.

 

Δ. Your eldest sister her name is Esémeli.  [Note: Dee.]  

 

 Ma. ..... My sister is not so short as you make her.

 

Δ. O, I cry you mercy, she is to be pronounced Eseméli.  [Note: Eseméli.]  

 

 E. K. She smileth, one calls her saying, Come away Maiden.

 

 Ma. ..... I will read over my Gentlewoemen first.

 

My Master Dee will teach me, if I say amisse.

 

Δ. Read over your Gentlewoemen as it pleaseth you.

 

 Ma. ..... I have Gentlemen and Gentlwoemen, Look you here.

 

 E- K. She bringeth a little book out of her pocket,

 

..... She pointeth to a in Picture the book.

 

 Mad. ..... Is not this a pretty man.

 

Δ. What is his name?

 

 Ma..... My ..... saith, his name is Edward, Look you, he hath a Crown upon his head, my Mother saith, that this man was Duke of York.

 

 E. K. She looketh upon a Picture in the Book with a Coronet in his hand and a Crown upon his head.

 

 Ma. ..... This was a jolly man when he was King of England.

 

Δ. How long since is it that he was King of England? 

 

 Ma. ..... Do you ask me such a question, I am but a little Maiden? Lo, here is his Father Richard Plantagenet, and his Father also.

 

Δ. How call you him?

 

 Ma. ..... Richard, Surely this was Richard Earle of Cambridge.

 

 E. K. She turneth the book leaves, and said.

 

 Mad. ..... Here is a grim Lord, He maketh me afraid.

 

Δ. Why doth he make you afraid?

 

 Ma. ..... He is a stern fellow, I do not know him what he is. But this was the Duke of Cla­rence. This was Father to Richard Earle of Cambridge. Lo, here is Anne his wife.

 

 E. K. Turning over the leafe,

 

The same was heir to all Mortimers lands.

 

 Edmund was her brother.

 

Lo, Sir, here be the wicked Mortimers. 

 

 E K. She turned over diverse leaves, and then she said

 

 Ma. ..... This same is Roger Mortimer. 

 

..... My Mother saith this man was Earl of the Marches. 

 

This same is his wife.

 

He had a great deale of lands by her, for she was an Heire. 

 

This same is wild Genvill, her Father.  [Note: Pronounced Jenville. ]  

 

Here is a Town they call Webley. Here is Beudley. Here is Mortimers Clybery. Here is wild Wenlock. Here is Ludlow. Here is Stanton Lacy. Genvill his wife was Heire of all these. Here is Hugh Lacy her Father. He weareth his haire long, for he was Deputy of Ire­land; That maketh him look with such a writhen face.

 

My sister hath torne out the other two leaves, I will bring them when you have supped.

 

I pray do not tell any body of me.

 

Δ. We were earnestly called for to Supper by my folks.  [Note: Nsta.]  

 

After Supper.

 

 Ma. ..... Here is William Lacy Father to Hugh. 

 

Here is Richard his Father. And here is Sir Richard his Father, and here is William, Sir Richards Brother. Here is his going into France. 

 

Δ. Quo anno Christi?

 

 Mad. ..... I warrant you my eldest Sister will tell you all. Here is his going into Denmark. 

 

My Sister will come shortly, and tell you how he married in Poland, and what issue this Wil­liam  [Note: Her eldest Sister. Her Sister is to tell the rest.]  had.

 

Δ. I pray declare the Pedigree down to this Albert Lascy. 

 

 Ma. ..... Alas, I cannot tell whats done in other Countries.

 

Δ. I know you are not Particular of this Country, but Universal for all countries in the whole world, which is indeed but one Countrey, or a great City, &c.

 

 Mad. ..... Well, my sister will shortly come and tell you unlooked for, If you judge these things well that I have spoken. Nam vera sunt. Nam verus est qui me mifit. 

 <!-- CARE_TEI_PAGE {"n": "3", "facs": "tcp:49588:45"} --> 

Truth is all that is truth.

 

The Mortimer I spake of, is the first of the six: there were six Mortimers Earles of March. Edmond was the last, and Roger the first; that Mortimer was the Grandfathers Grandfather of this Edmond. 

 

 E. K. There seemeth some one to call her, whom I hear now.

 

 Ma ..... I come.

 

Δ. She took up her Skrolls on the ground, of which some were very old, and she put up her book.

 

 Ma ..... This may stand you in some stead.

 

Δ. Mitte lucem tuam & veritatem tuam, Jesu Christe, Lux vera, & veritatis perennis Fons. Amen. 

 

[Figure in source: ]  

Monday à Meridie hora 4½ 

 

Δ. We presented our selves, ready for instruction receiving, and presumed not to call my  [Note:  Junii 2, 1583.]  good Minister spiritual, but by humble prayer referred all to God his good pleasure.

 

 E K. The Golden Curtain which covereth all the Stone hangeth still, but I heare a voice or sentence thrice repeated, thus.

 

 A voice ..... Sanctum, Signatum, & ad tempus.

 

Δ. The sense hereof may be divers wayes understood, and more then I can imagine, but which sense is to our instruction would I faine know.

 

 A voice. ..... Sanctum, quia hoc velle suum; sigillatum quia determinatum ad tempus.

 

 E K. Hard speeches, but he could not perfectly discern them.

 

 A voice ..... Ad tempus & ad tempus (inquam) quia rerum consummatio. All things are at hand. 

 

The Seat is prepared.

 

Justice hath determined.

 

The Judge is not yet willing.

 

Mercy thrusteth it self betwixt the Divinity. But it is said,

 

The Time shall be shortned.

 

 E K. Saw no creature: But the voice came behind him over his head, till now: when he espied one standing on the Table besides the silke cloth on which the Stone stood; he seemed like a Husbandman all in red apparel, red hose close to his legs, a red jacket, red buttoned cap on his head, yea, and red shooes. He asked E. K. how he did, and E. K. answered, Well I thank God.

 

Δ. By your apparel it should seem you have somewhat to say concerning the Commons of this Realme, and not of high School-points, or Sciences. I am desirous to know who sent you? What is your message? and what is your name? for a name you have peculiar as all Creatures else.

 

Δ. He paused a good while; whereupon I asked him if he considered my speeches?

 

..... I consider your speeches, for I have left nothing behind.

 

 E. K. He kneeleth down and seemeth to say somewhat, his speech is quick, round, and ready. He seemeth to pray in a strange Language. I per­ceived these words among many other, Oh Gahire Rudna gephna oh Gahire, &c.

 

His Countenance was directed towards the Stone.

 

..... Vestra non mea facio.

 <!-- CARE_TEI_PAGE {"n": "4", "facs": "tcp:49588:46"} --> 

 E K Now he standeth up.

 

..... Hast not thou said, From whom comest thou? What is thy message? [Δ. He looked to­ward me] And hast urged my name? Saying, All things have a name. It is true; for so they have because they are. Hast thou left any thing unsaid?  [Note: Δ. All things have a name, vide  〈◊〉  Tert. parte libri Eraconiersis de 30 Aeris ex­ercitibus. The summe of our command­ed observa­tion. Note 7.]  

 

Δ. You rehearse my speeches not onely in general, but also in particular.

 

The will of God be done (to his glory) for the rest.

 

..... My message is from him, in whose name thou hast desired it, which hath said lift up thine eyes, and look unto (behold I say) the sum of my Commandments, 1. What I am, 2. Whose Mini­sters you are, and (as it is said before) 3. To what end and purpose it is.

 

Then cease to plead when Judgement standeth in place; For all things are determined already. The 7 doores are opened. The 7 Governours have almost ended their Government. 

 

The Earth laboureth as sick, yea sick unto death.

 

The Waters pour forth weepings, and have not moisture sufficient to quench their own sorrows.

 

The Aire withereth, for her heat is infected.

 

The Fire consumeth and is scalded with his own heat.

 

The B dies above are ready to say, We are weary of our courses.

 

Nature would fain creep again into the bosom of her good and gracious Master.

 

Darknesse is now heavy and sinketh down together: She hath builded her self, yea (I say) she hath advanced her self into a mighty building she saith, Have done, for I am ready to receive my burden.

 

Hell it self is weary of Earth: For why? The son of Darknesse cometh now to challenge his right: and seeing all things prepared and provided, desireth to establish himself a kingdom; say­ing,  [Note: Antichrist his saying in the spir it of Satan.]  We are now stronge enough, Let us now build us a kingdom upon earth, and Now establish that which we could not confirm above. 

 

And therefore, Behold the end.

 

When the time cometh, The ..... thy sorrows shall be greater than the sweetnesse, the sorrows  [Note: Sorrows.]  (I mean) of that thou seest; I mean in respect of the sweetnesse of thy knowledge. Then will you lament and weep for tho e thou thoughtst were just men.

 

When you earnestly pray it shall be said unto you Labor. When you would take Mercy Justice  [Note: Labor.]  shall say, Be it so.

 

Therefore (I say) thirst not overmnch: For fear least thy capacity be confounded.

 

Neither move thou him which hath moved all things already to the end.

 

But do  〈◊〉  that which is commanded.

 

Neither prescribe thou any form to God his building.

 

All things shall be brought into an uniformal Order.  [Note: Al. alasky.]  

 

Whom thou sayest that thou hast not yet confirmed, confirm with good counsel. It is said I have accepted him.

 

Are not these News sufficient?

 

It is said,  〈◊〉  shall govern me a people: of himself he cannot. Therefore let him believe, and secondly Rejoyce that the Angel of God hath so governed him. That in Election he shall  [Note: Notes in E­lection.]  govern him a people.

 

Desireth he to hear of greater blessednesse?

 

He hath also said: Then shall it be said unto him, O King.  [Note:  O King. Vide tamen de ejus juturo casu in actionibus de Lask. Pride. ]  

 

It followeth consequently that he is called, and that to a Kingly Office: For whosoever is An­nointed in the Lord, his Kingdom is for ever. 

 

Will he be the son of perdition? Let him then with his fathers put on the garments of pride. 

 

Desireth he news? Tell him thou hast prayed for him; the Devil envyeth him, and his estate. 

 

Tell him that I say so.

 

Say it is a shame for a Kings Son to commit theft; and for him that is called, to do the workes of unrighteousnesse. Studiest thou to please him? Give him sharp and wholesome counsel. For in him (I fay) the state and alteration of the whole World shall begin.

 

Wouldst thou know from whence I came? Thoushalt.

 

  〈◊〉  it Humbly, it is not my part to meddle any further than my charge.

 

But as it is said before unto thee, So shall it come to passe.

 

 Moses had a rod whereby he was known, and the hand of God approved.

 

Let him use therefore to carry the rod of righteousnesse about him.

 

For we are seven: and in us is comprehended that rod wherewith Moses wrought. As it is be­gun  [Note:  Moses 7. rod. Sanctum, signa­tum, ad tempus.]  so I end: What ye see here is   〈◊〉   [pointing to the ..... and by him sealed and for until the time. 

 

Therefore use patience herein until the time that it is said unto thee ..... 

 

 Venite, videte, (& loquimini) Judicia mea.

 

He that saith thus (I speak of my self, and as concerning my message,) is equal with the great­est Angels, and his name is Murifri. 

 

Thou hast written my name, and I am of thy Kalender, because thy Kalender is of God.  [Note:  Murifri my Calender.]  

 

In the grounds of all thy Tables thou shalt finde my name.

 

Δ. I remember not any such name written by me, but it may be contained in some new Composition, or Collection.

 

 Mur. ..... It is true, for if thou badst remembred all those things which thou hast written, then should not my message need.

 <!-- CARE_TEI_PAGE {"n": "5", "facs": "tcp:49588:46"} --> 

Δ. If I might without offending you, I would move two Petitions unto you, one concerning the Soul, and the other concerning the body: Concerning the Soul, is for one Isabel Lister, whom the wicked Enemy hath sore afflicted long with dangerous temptations, and hath brought her knives to destroy her self withall; she resisteth hitherto, and desireth my helping counsel, which how small it is God knoweth. The other is of another woman, who hath great need, and is driven to maintain her self, her husband, and three children by her hand la­bour, and there is one that by dream is advertised of a place of Treasure hid in a Cellar, which this woman hath hired thereupon, and hath no longer time of hiring the said Cellar, but till Midsummer next. She, and this dreaming Maiden digged somewhat, and found certain to­kens notefied unto her: But so left off. I would gladly have your help herein, if it pleased God.

 

 Mur. ..... I answer thee, I will come again soon, and thou shalt receive a Medecine which shall teach thee to work help in the first. The second is vanity, for it is not so, but to the intent that after great hope of this world hath infected the weaklings minde: Desperation might have the more open and ready entrance. But yet she shall be comforted for thy sake.

 

Δ. The praise be unto God.

 

 Mur. ..... I Go. One thing I have to say, be faithfull in all things.

 

I have said.

 

Δ. I prayed, and gave thanks hartily to God for his mercies, and graces, and so rose up.

 

Δ. Then he said write, M. 49. under V. 43 under R. 35. 1. and 47. under F. 9. R. 33. I. 42 This shal lead thee to my name, he that sent me be amongst yon. Δ. Amen, Amen, Amen.

 

Δ. Note in Tabula Collecta, (which I first gathered of the 49. good Angels) I took the third letters out of the names, it is to wit, out of the 49th. name, and th..... 47. 9 33. 42. which agreed very well with the letters, but the five and thirtieth name did not yield R. in his third letter. Therefore I am. .... in the.....

 

Monday after supper 1583.  [Note: Junii 3. ]  

 

Δ. After supper, as we were together in my study, and attending somewhat the return of the good messager spiritual, and said that he promised to come again suddenly, he appeared and answered.

 

 Mur. ..... So I am, write 7. 30.25. 44.37.35 46.

 

To the first S. to the second O. the third L. the fourth G. the fifth A. the sixth R. the 7th. S. 

 

Δ. That maketh SOLGARS. 

 

 Mur..... Add the first, and last number together, it maketh 53. let that be the Centre to the rest.

 

Δ. To be put to the Center of the Steptagonum. 

 

 Mur. ..... So. The ground hereof is to be found in the third. Table in the first book: I mean in  [Note: The third Ta­b • e in the first book.]  the third of the seven, the Table of B. B. &c. being the first.

 

My name is also to be found in the same Table.

 

Form this upon a plate of lead: It prevaileth as a cure against such infections. My promise is done.

 

Δ. How is this to be used?

 

 Mur. ..... Vse it upon the body molested, adding the letters of her name in a small Circle on the back half, not the letters in their forms expressed, but the number of such letters.

 

Δ. We know not how to number her name in our letters.

 

 Mur. ..... Take them out of the second Table (any Table else of the seventh will serve) so that  [Note: Δ The second Table did not serve, & there­fore I used the seventh, where all the letters might be had.]  thou take the numbers as thou findest them placed with the letters.

 

Δ. How is this to be used about her body?

 

 Mur. ..... As by discretion shall be thought best: It prevaileth sufficiently, so it be done, but thus far I teach thee, and this, as concerning nature.

 

The health of him which sent me be amongst you. Amen.

 

Δ. Gloria & gratiarum actio perennis sit Deo nostro omnipotenti uni & Trino, Amen. 

[Figure in source:  

## The fore­part of the Lamin.

 ]  

[Figure in source:  

## Isabel Li­ster, the back part of the La­min.

 ]  

 

Wednesday a Meridie circa 2d. 1583.  [Note: Junii 5. ]  

 

Δ. E. K. Had been ever since nine of the Clock in the morning in a marvellous great dis­quietnesse of minde, fury, and rage, by reason his brother Thomas had brought him news that <!-- CARE_TEI_PAGE {"n": "6", "facs": "tcp:49588:47"} --> a Commission was out to attache, and apprehend him as a fellon for coyning of money. Second­ly,  [Note: A meer un­truth in every part thereof, and a malici­ous lye.]  that his wife was gone from Mistresse Freemans house at Blohley, and how Mr. Husey had reported him to be a cosener, and had used very bitter and grievous reports of him now of late; and that his wife was at home with her mother at Chipping Norton, whereupon, I considering his great disorder and incumbrance toward him externally, and his greater offending of God with his furious impatience internally; and remembring the whole premises of God his ser­vice to be performed by us two (if we would be dutifull servants to his Divine Majesty) I was touched with a great pang of Compassion, both that any Christian should use such speeches as he used, or be of so revenging a minde and intent as he shewed himself to be: and also in respect of mine own credit to be brought in doubt, for embracing the company of such an one, a disorderly person: And thirdly, that the good service of God might hereby be taken from our two executing, to our great danger, both in body and soul: Therefore to do my duty as a man resolute (upon our uniting for Gods service) to do for him as for my self: I made  [Note:   〈◊◊〉  communia.]  God my refuge for comfort, counsel, and help in this great affliction, and crosse of tempta­tion.

 

Whereupon after my vehement and humble prayers for the foresaid purpose, this voyce was heard of E. K. 

 

I had (upon some reasonable respect) set the shew-stone with the mystery in it, on the Table by E. K. also.

 

A voyce. ..... Let the daughters of light

This Letter being now written, and not yet folded up, my friend E. K. was ready and came out of his Chamber into my Study; and I told him, that I was even now sending word to the Prince Laskie of his rideing out, and return after five dayes; and so shewed him the Letter: who when he came to the phrase, Quid sit ipsa veritas, he was samewhat offended, saying, What secret meaning hath this, upon some of your two former conference? Truly (said I) even such as the circumstance of the Letter doth import, that is; Whereas you said that you intended to return within five dayes, or at the same dayes end, it is uncertain whether you will, or shall, return later or sooner: and therefore Quid sit ipsa veritas of your return, or intent to return, onely God doth know. He would by no meanes admit that my sincere exposition, but seemed suspitious of some other undue constructions of those former words; thereupon I took the Letter and tore it in three pieces, and sent none: But in my mind re­ferred all to God his disposition, assuring my self of God his most constant proceeding in his own affairs. Shortly after said E. K. to me, Certainly here is a spiritual Creature in my right shoulder, who sensibly saith to me, Come away: So (said I) did one say to Sowle, when  [Note:  Sowle. Evil spirits.]  they would have had him away to have drowned him, whom I stayed in this Study by force, and so hindered the Devil of his purpose then; as appeareth by that unhappy man yet alive. Nay said E. K. they have told me that if I tarry here, I shall be hanged; and if I go with this Prince he will cut off my head, and that you mean not to keep promise with me; And therefore if I might have a thousand pound to tarry, yea a Kingdom, I cannot: Therefore I release you of your promise of 50 pounds yearly Stipend to me, and you need not doubt but God will de­fend  [Note: Fifty pound yearly stipend.]  you and prosper you, and can of the very stones raise up children to Abraham: And a­gain I cannot abide my wife, I love her not, nay I abhor her; and there in the house I am misli­ked,  [Note:  E.
